papers.title: Neural Costate Guidance for Autonomous Cislunar Low-Thrust Trajectory Generation
papers.summary: Future missions will benefit from onboard autonomous low-thrust trajectory generation to correct deviations from the nominal flight path caused by navigation errors and thruster outages. Onboard computing resources rarely allow the solution of a cold-started, long-duration nonconvex optimal control problem, especially in dynamically challenging regions such as the cislunar to translunar corridor of the Earth-Moon system. This paper develops data augmentation and training techniques that enable a neural network to predict accurate initial costates of the indirect method. A recovery trajectory is then built from repeated network queries in a computationally efficient guidance algorithm. Training data are produced by the backward generation of optimal examples method, extending prior approaches to the circular restricted three-body problem. A novel anchor trajectory approach is developed to cover the relevant state space, and costate rescaling and a Hamiltonian loss term are used to improve learning. The method is demonstrated on Earth-Moon transfers from a high Earth orbit to halo orbits about L1 and L2. Under navigation errors and thruster outages, a spacecraft reaches the target orbit more often with the proposed method than with nominal-trajectory tracking or fully numerical reoptimization. Onboard computation is reduced by more than an order of magnitude compared with reoptimization.

papers.title: Neural-Network Approximators for Low-Thrust Multi-Asteroid Rendezvous Optimization
papers.summary: Designing low-thrust multi-asteroid rendezvous missions requires the coupled selection of asteroid sequences, encounter epochs, and low-thrust trajectories. Lambert transfers support rapid beam search but do not directly describe thrust-limited transfer capacity or propellant consumption. This paper develops two complementary low-thrust neural approximators. The first directly predicts the continuous maximum admissible initial mass from numerically optimized low-thrust transfers, providing a transfer-capacity estimate for comparison with the current spacecraft mass. The second predicts mass-dependent propellant consumption and propagates spacecraft mass to subsequent legs. With the carefully-designed input features and network structure, the approximators reduce mean absolute errors by 72.2% and 75.5%, respectively, relative to conventional deep neural network baselines. These predictions are incorporated into a Lambert-ranked beam search through resource filtering and recursive mass propagation before final beam selection. The method is evaluated on fixed-visit, maximum-visit, and deployment-collection missions. Across the tested cases, the proposed resource filtering increases the fraction of candidate sequences that yield accepted low-thrust solutions, raises the maximum validated asteroid-visit count by up to 15.4%, and improves the best mission objective by up to 17.8%. These results demonstrate that continuous transfer-capacity and propellant predictions can improve finite-width sequence search.

papers.title: Predicting the Orbital Retention of Habitable-Zone Planets Following Stellar Flybys Using Machine Learning
papers.summary: Stellar flybys can significantly alter the orbital configurations of planetary systems, potentially displacing planets initially located within the habitable zone (HZ) of their host stars. In this study, we investigate the dynamical effects of stellar encounters on HZ planets using a large suite of three-body N-body simulations. We examine how the properties of the host star, passing star, planetary orbit, and encounter geometry influence the final orbital configuration. A planet is considered to retain an HZ orbit only if it remains bound to its original host and its entire final orbital range, from periastron to apastron, lies within the HZ boundaries. Based on the simulation results, we develop an XGBoost classifier to predict the final HZ status of planets following stellar encounters. The model achieves an accuracy of 0.90, an ROC-AUC of 0.97, and a PR-AUC of 0.97 on the test set. Feature importance analysis identifies the encounter-impulse parameter as the dominant predictor of the outcome. The classifier provides a computational speedup of approximately 74 compared with direct N-body simulations. We further evaluate the model using an independent dataset representing a globular-cluster environment, where approximately 20 per cent of planets retain HZ orbits. Despite the naturally imbalanced class distribution, the model achieves an accuracy of 0.87, an ROC-AUC of 0.92, and a PR-AUC of 0.77. These results demonstrate the potential of machine learning for efficiently predicting the dynamical retention of HZ planets following stellar encounters and for investigating their outcomes in dense stellar environments.

papers.title: Operator-Valued Q-Learning: Compositional Bellman Recursions for Order-Sensitive Decision Making
papers.summary: In quantum pulse sequences, spacecraft attitude control and in-hand reorientation, actions act on a hidden physical state as non-commuting operators, so the outcome of a plan depends on the order of its actions. We let the value function carry this structure: each Q(s,a) is an N x N operator, and the Bellman backup applies the action's dual map to the continuation value, Q(s,a) = K_a^*(R(s,a) + gamma E V(s')). Unrolled along a plan, the recursion builds the ordered product of the actions' operators, and the value at any latent state is a linear trace readout. It is exact for policies that do not observe the latent, the backup contracts for unitary and orthogonal dynamics, and an asynchronous operator TD scheme learns it with almost-sure convergence. Classical values live in a lattice, so a maximum over actions exists; self-adjoint operators form an anti-lattice (Kadison) and have none. An operator log-sum-exp still gives one operator per state-action pair whose readout upper-bounds the value of every policy at every latent state. The sampled update converges to it for a finite horizon, and it reduces to soft Q-learning and the QMDP bound when actions commute. We prove that scalar values on observations that ignore action order must confuse swapped histories, that exact history tables grow exponentially for free action groups but polynomially for nilpotent ones, and give a Hankel-rank lower bound on the operator dimension. In experiments the learned policy matches 1000-simulation tree search on SO(3) pointing for horizons up to 20 at ~10^4 times lower decision cost, transfers zero-shot to unseen initial states, and acts exactly on its belief mean when the initial state is hidden, where plugging the mean into a DQN does not. A planner with the same model knowledge is more sample-efficient at short horizons, and a DQN given the operators matches or exceeds OpQ.

papers.title: MASTO: Missed-thrust Aware Stochastic Trajectory Optimization
papers.summary: Missed Thrust Events (MTEs) are a major roadblock towards widespread adoption of low-thrust propulsion for deep space missions. Unplanned thruster outages have previously been difficult to directly incorporate in the preliminary mission design process, and current approaches mostly introduce robustness by conservative heuristics such as mandatory coasting arcs, which do not possess any safety guarantees, and usually only consider one missed-thrust event. Therefore, in this work, we utilize a stochastic hybrid system framework to model a spacecraft as a Markov jump system that can switch between nominal and failure mode. We formulate the Missed-thrust resilient trajectory optimization problem as a Markov jump covariance steering problem, and propose a sequential convex programming-based approach, which can also respect chance constraints. We demonstrate our framework on two complex three-dimensional transfers in the Earth-Moon circular restricted three body problem, showcasing robustness against a range of MTEs, while respecting chance constraints. We further analyze controller performance across a range of MTE-probability distributions, offering valuable insights into the MTE-resilient trajectory design trade space.

papers.title: WingBench: Benchmarking How AI Agents Search for Better Designs
papers.summary: Design search often uses cheap learned predictions to choose which candidates deserve expensive tests, but these tests can fail, especially on the unusual designs that optimization favors. We introduce WingBench, a multifidelity benchmark in which optimizers and AI agents design transonic wings with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) inside the search. They can query a learned aerodynamic surrogate and spend a fixed budget of sequential CFD evaluations, each returning a score or a failure type. WingBench grades the design each method recommends, reporting separately whether it receives a valid score and how good that score is. Using WingBench, we contribute a study of five baseline optimizers and a comparison of three AI agent methods, which produced 6,629 CFD evaluation records. Feedback helps baseline optimizers deliver valid designs when it changes their later proposals, but the differential-evolution variant does so with lower aerodynamic quality. An open-ended research agent finds designs of similar quality to the strongest baselines over 32 CFD queries, with different prior information and unmatched total computation. In early search, our reflection and planning implementations do not consistently improve on it. We release the data, code, agent prompts, and analysis scripts for reproducibility.
papers.title_ja: WingBench: AIエージェントによる設計探索のベンチマーク

papers.title: Verifying the Outputs of PDE Solvers: From Finite Elements to Neural Surrogates
papers.summary: Physics simulation outputs increasingly come from solvers that no expert inspects, such as third-party packages in automated pipelines, programs written by large language models (LLMs), and learned surrogates. In earlier work on cardiac pulsed field ablation, we proposed that solvers return a certificate with their answers. The certificate consists of an admissible potential and an exactly charge-conserving current, and a small independent checker turns it into guaranteed error bounds against a written specification of the physics. Here, the same checker verifies the outputs of other solvers on the same problem. Specifically, FEniCSx computes both fields and receives the same bounds as our own solver. Five plausible bugs in a correct solver, one of them about 0.2% from the true impedance, all converge and pass a grid convergence study, yet the certificate rejects or refutes all five. Of three solvers written by LLMs, one is correct and certified to 0.1%, and one never solves the equation but converges. Neural networks that predict the coefficients of a reduced basis emit admissible fields and receive valid per-prediction bounds, at most 0.0021% wide inside their training range and 0.3-25% wide outside it, where 90% conformal intervals cover none of 14 tests. Untuned Fourier neural operators with free nodal outputs receive valid but uninformative bounds. On a uniform grid, interpolation onto the certificate grid limits them, and on the certificate grid, thin cells turn small nodal errors into large energy errors. Energy-norm training narrows the certified interval tenfold, and projecting the nodal-loss outputs onto the reduced basis narrows it by two to four orders of magnitude, still uninformative. The guarantee concerns the stated model and holds for any output, wherever its input lies. It is informative only when the output is accurate in energy on a grid that resolves the problem.

papers.title: Expressive Shallow Networks for Physics-Informed Learning: Why Curvature-Aware Optimization and FP64 Are Not Enough
papers.summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often struggle with high-frequency and high-order partial differential equations (PDEs) due to optimization stiffness and spectral bias, despite possessing sufficient approximation capacity. Existing remedies, including modified feature representations, domain decomposition, higher floating-point precision, and curvature-aware optimizers, can improve convergence but largely act as workarounds for optimization difficulties arising from deep architectures rather than addressing their underlying source. We investigate Physics-Informed Shallow Universal Polynomial Networks (PI-SUPNs), which replace deep nonlinear compositions with learnable polynomial expansions, retaining high approximation capacity within a shallow computational graph. On a high-frequency Helmholtz benchmark, PI-SUPNs are the only architecture to successfully recover the solution, while all competing models fail even under FP64 precision and curvature-aware optimization. However, experiments on higher vibrational modes of a fourth-order Euler-Bernoulli beam reveal that architectural improvements alone are insufficient: accurate solutions require the combination of PI-SUPNs, FP64 precision, and curvature-aware optimization. Additionally, Allen-Cahn experiments show that PI-SUPNs achieve lower solution and derivative errors at reduced computational cost, with more favorable loss landscapes than competing architectures. We also establish quasi-local approximation properties and spline-based convergence bounds for SUPNs. Our results show that shallow network architectures are an important mechanism for improving physics-informed trainability, but accurate solutions to the most challenging PDEs can still require FP64 precision and curvature-aware optimization.
papers.title_ja: 物理情報学習のための表現力豊かな浅層ネットワーク：曲率認識型最適化とFP64が不十分な理由

papers.title: IADR: Interface-Augmented Neural Operator for Phase-Field Mean-Curvature Flow
papers.summary: The Allen-Cahn equation is one of the standard phase-field models for mean-curvature flow (MCF), parameterised by the diffuse-interface width $\varepsilon$. Practical simulations span a range of $\varepsilon$, so a single model covering this range is needed. PDE-specific neural operators are accurate but must be retrained at every $\varepsilon$; general neural operators cover $\varepsilon$ in one model but lose the phase-field structure of the target. We introduce Interface-Augmented Diffusion-Reaction (IADR), a neural operator that addresses both shortcomings: a target network with a diffusion-and-reaction (DR) structure preserves the phase-field structure of the Allen-Cahn equation, while a hypernetwork that maps $\varepsilon$ to the weights of this target network amortises the dependence on $\varepsilon$ across the range. A single IADR matches the per-$\varepsilon$ specialists on in-distribution data within the prescribed range, retains their cross-shape generalisation under both $\varepsilon$- and geometry-out-of-distribution shifts, and retains their compact DR target structure with millisecond-scale inference. We further establish a conditional $K$-step rollout error bound under consistency and stability assumptions.

papers.title: FMSNO: Scaling Surface Neural Operators by Learned Flow Matching Reparametrisation
papers.summary: We propose the Flow Matching Surface Neural Operator (FMSNO), which combines learning a shared map from irregular surface meshes to a regular two-dimensional grid on the sphere and training a neural operator on the regular grid. Constructing a separate map for each new geometry can dominate inference time on large meshes. We initially pretrain the mapping by flow matching using precomputed optimal transport maps as targets and then continue its training using combined geometry and CFD objectives. We apply it to unseen geometries in a single forward pass. The learned flow deforms the surface points, and we project its endpoints onto the sphere. We then splat geometric features onto the spherical grid, apply a neural operator (we tested both Fourier and Spherical Fourier Neural Operators), and interpolate its output back to the surface. For a mesh with $N$ points, evaluating the map costs O(N), and the full prediction costs O(NlogN) with the FNO backbone. We evaluate surface pressure prediction on ShapeNet-Car, AhmedML, and DrivAerNet++, and drag coefficient prediction on DrivAerNet++. Across the three pressure benchmarks, our accuracy is on par with that of the most accurate baseline. On a surface with one million points, our method achieves a 354x end-to-end inference speedup over that baseline while keeping the same memory usage asymptotics of O(N).

papers.title: Bayesian Optimization for Inhomogeneous Functions via Locally Adaptive Kernels
papers.summary: Bayesian optimization (BO) is a powerful and general framework for sample-efficient global optimization. Most BO methods rely on stationary Gaussian processes, implicitly assuming that an objective black-box function exhibits homogeneous smoothness across the input space. However, many complex real-world functions have highly inhomogeneous regularity, exhibiting both smooth and rough behavior. This fundamental mismatch between the model and the black-box function severely degrades both sample efficiency and surrogate accuracy of BO. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the Inhomogeneous Bayesian optimization framework. We develop a partitioned modeling strategy that dynamically subdivides the search space into subdomains, capturing spatially varying smoothness through locally adaptive kernels. To dynamically adjust the spatial resolution of the surrogate model, this approach utilizes a recursive splitting criterion. Furthermore, we develop a sampling allocation theory, establishing that driving the regional acquisition suprema below a common target level is achieved by polynomially denser sampling in rougher subdomains. Numerical experiments across homogeneous functions, synthetic inhomogeneous functions, and a real-world 8-dimensional LASSO hyperparameter tuning task demonstrate that our approach improves optimization efficiency on synthetic inhomogeneous functions, while performing comparably to Classic BO on homogeneous functions and on the LASSO task. This demonstrates the robustness of the adaptive partitioning mechanism.
papers.title_ja: 局所適応カーネルを用いた非均質関数へのベイズ最適化

papers.title: Physics-Informed Fusion-MIONet with IFENN: A Generalized Framework for Coupled Poroelasticity Problems
papers.summary: Complex, high-dimensional, large-scale poroelasticity simulations using traditional numerical solvers can be prohibitively expensive in terms of computational resources. We introduce an innovative framework for poroelasticity problems that integrates physics-informed machine learning (PI-ML) models with high-performance FEM solvers. This integration is achieved through the Integrated Finite Element Neural Network (IFENN) setup, which uses a staggered scheme between an FEM solver for mechanical equilibrium and a PI-ML model for fluid-flow predictions. We introduce a novel Physics-Informed Fusion-MIONet (PIF-MIONet) architecture, in which a fusion network encodes the outputs of the MIONet branches. The MIONet encodes different input functions, and the fusion network enables early interaction between the inputs, supporting generalization across multiple scenarios while adhering to the underlying physics of the poroelasticity problem. We study different examples, covering 2D and 3D domains and considering variable material properties and time discretizations. We test the models on unseen loading histories, demonstrating accuracy and generalizability across scenarios. For complex geometries and boundary conditions, we show that with both physics and data considered in the loss function, a PI-ML model can be trained using only 0.1\% of the training increments used for pure data-driven training. In addition, we expand the PIF-MIONet to incorporate a domain decomposition approach, which was found to be particularly useful when modeling flow over more complex geometries with more localized phenomena. For the first time, IFENN is implemented using the open-source multiphysics simulator GEOS for the FEM part, providing a path for the framework's application to industrial-scale simulations and complex multiphysics problems.
papers.title_ja: IFENNを用いた物理情報融合MIONet：結合ポロエラスティシティ問題のための汎用フレームワーク
papers.summary_ja: 高次元・大規模なポロエラスティシティシミュレーションの計算コスト削減を目的とし、物理情報機械学習（PI-ML）と高性能FEMソルバを統合したIFENNフレームワークを提案する。MIONetと融合ネットワークを組み合わせた新アーキテクチャPIF-MIONetにより、入力間の早期相互作用を実現し、物理法則に準拠しつつ多様なシナリオへの汎化性能を確保した。損失関数に物理とデータを含めることで、純粋なデータ駆動型学習の0.1%の訓練ステップで高精度なモデル訓練が可能であることを示した。さらに、オープンソースマルチフィジックスシミュレータGEOSとの統合により、産業規模の複雑なマルチフィジックス問題への適用経路を提示している。

papers.title: Transfer Learning and Experience Replay for Automotive Aerodynamic Surrogates
papers.summary: Neural surrogates enable rapid prediction of automotive aerodynamic fields, but achieving high accuracy often demands extensive computational fluid dynamics datasets. Generating these datasets for each new vehicle program or expansion of the design space can require prolonged simulation campaigns. Reusing knowledge from existing simulations offers a way to limit this burden, provided that models adapt to unfamiliar geometries while maintaining predictive accuracy. This study evaluated transfer learning and experience replay in two independent automotive aerodynamics experiments using a mesh-free neural surrogate. First, models pretrained on 1,981 sport utility vehicle cases from SHIFT-SUV were fine-tuned on subsets of the SHIFT-Truck pickup dataset. Target training-set size was varied from 100 to 613 cases across the surface-only and joint surface and volume configurations to assess data efficiency. Fine-tuning reduced every reported field mean absolute error (MAE) relative to training from scratch at the same target budget. For joint surface and volume prediction, fine-tuning on 100 truck cases matched or improved on all four field MAEs obtained by training from scratch on 200 cases. Second, an independently trained model learned a base task using 332 DrivAerML cases and was adapted to a novel task using 31 cases with a previously unseen combination of design features. Experience replay incorporated cases from the base-task training set during adaptation. Full replay lowered field errors on 45 held-out base-task designs by approximately 36% to 42% relative to adaptation without replay; retaining half the base-task training set yielded reductions of approximately 30% to 35%. Together, these findings support transfer learning and experience replay as complementary strategies for data-efficient neural surrogate development across successive engineering tasks.
papers.title_ja: 自動車空力サロゲートモデルにおける転移学習と経験リプレイ
papers.summary_ja: 自動車空力場の予測において、計算流体力学（CFD）データ生成のコストを削減するため、転移学習と経験リプレイの効果を評価した。SUVデータで事前学習したモデルをトラックデータでファインチューニングすることで、スクラッチ学習より少ないデータ量で同等以上の精度を達成した。また、新タスクへの適応時にベースタスクのデータをリプレイすることで、ベースタスクの精度低下を約30〜42%抑制した。これらは、連続するエンジニアリングタスク間でデータ効率の高いニューラルサロゲート開発を実現する補完的な戦略であることを示している。

papers.title: RefineKV: Query-Adaptive KV Cache Compression via Attention-Error Bounds
papers.summary: Repeatedly accessing the full key--value (KV) cache is a major bottleneck in long-context language model decoding. We find that small query-specific subsets can accurately approximate full attention, yet their union covers nearly the entire cache, motivating query-adaptive access for the KV cache. A natural approach is to split the KV cache into clusters, using compact representatives for clusters that incur negligible error while expanding the rest to their original KV entries. We derive a selection criterion from an upper bound on attention-output error, which reveals two complementary factors governing the error: importance measures the impact of a cluster, while distortion measures how faithfully the cluster can be represented. Based on this criterion, we propose RefineKV, a decoding-time query-adaptive KV compression method. Experiments on two models and three benchmarks demonstrate that RefineKV retains near-full-attention quality while achieving up to 7.6x speedup in the attention phase and 1.66x faster decoding, establishing a new quality-latency Pareto frontier.
papers.title_ja: RefineKV: 注意誤差の上限に基づくクエリ適応型KVキャッシュ圧縮
papers.summary_ja: 長文脈LLMのデコーディングにおけるKVキャッシュアクセスのボトルネックを解決するため、クエリごとに適応的にKVキャッシュを圧縮する手法RefineKVを提案する。注意出力の誤差上限から導出された選択基準を用い、重要度と歪みを考慮してクラスタを代表値で近似するか展開するかを決定する。2つのモデルと3つのベンチマークでの実験により、ほぼ完全な注意品質を維持しつつ、注意フェーズで最大7.6倍、デコーディング全体で1.66倍の高速化を実現し、品質と遅延の新たなパレートフロンティアを確立した。

papers.title: Selection Policies for Equal-Byte Mixed-Precision Quantization of Small Language Models
papers.summary: Can changing which matrices receive 2, 4, or 8 bits improve a small language model without increasing its parameter storage? I compare two parent-selection rules in the same genetic algorithm: a binary-tournament variant and an Alternis-inspired rule. A separate baseline samples repaired random allocations without crossover or mutation. All three use the same MLX affine quantizer, byte ceiling, initialization and candidate allowance within each study. An exploratory study on Qwen3.5-2B evaluates 90 allocations per run. The main study on Qwen3-1.7B evaluates 500 distinct allocations per run over 10 paired seeds. Against uniform four-bit, tournament reduces held-out next-token negative log-likelihood (NLL) by 0.0616 on AG News and 0.0152 on IMDb on average, improving all 10 seeds on each corpus at identical parameter storage. Alternis improves five seeds and ties five on AG News; on IMDb its mean gain is near zero. Random returns uniform four-bit in every seed. The tournament representative answers 156 of 400 ARC-Challenge questions correctly versus 163 for uniform; no accuracy gain is demonstrated on this subset. The result favors this tournament variant for text prediction under the tested protocol, not for compression ratio or task accuracy.
papers.title_ja: 小型言語モデルにおける等バイト混合精度量子化のための選択ポリシー
papers.summary_ja: 小型LLMの混合精度量子化において、遺伝的アルゴリズムを用いてどの行列に2/4/8ビットを割り当てるかを最適化する手法を提案する。Qwen3-1.7Bモデルを対象に、トーナメント方式の選択ルールが均一4ビット量子化と比較して、パラメータ保存量を変えずに次トークン予測のNLLを改善することを示した。一方、ARC-Challengeなどのタスク精度では明確な向上は確認されず、テキスト予測性能の向上に特化した結果である。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの量子化と効率化というユーザーの関心と直接一致する。

papers.title: PAMS: Preconditioned Activation-Metric Subspace for Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-tuning
papers.summary: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization provides a computationally efficient approach to fine-tuning large language models (LLMs), but conventional methods typically rely on isotropic perturbations that ignore the anisotropic structure of neural-network parameter spaces. We introduce Preconditioned Activation-Metric Subspace (PAMS), a ZO optimization framework that uses forward-pass activation statistics to construct structured, layer-wise perturbation geometries without computing gradients or forming dense curvature matrices. PAMS tracks a low-rank approximation of the dominant activation subspace and its associated spectrum online, and uses the spectrum to softly reweight perturbation variance while preserving exploration in directions outside the retained subspace. A trace normalization separates the perturbation geometry from its overall scale, enabling consistent perturbation magnitudes across layers. We show theoretically that the resulting perturbation covariance induces right-side preconditioning of the gradient of the corresponding Gaussian-smoothed objective. We further characterize the estimator's smoothing bias and second moment and derive a nonconvex convergence guarantee that captures the effects of the perturbation geometry and smoothing radius. The proposed low-rank tracking procedure requires $\mathcal{O}(n_l r)$ persistent memory for a layer with input dimension nl and retained rank r, avoiding the $\mathcal{O}(n_l^2)$ memory required by a dense activation covariance. Experiments on transformer-based language-model fine-tuning tasks across GLUE and SuperGLUE demonstrate that PAMS improves the effectiveness and stability of zeroth-order optimization while retaining its gradient-free and objective-evaluation-based advantages.
papers.title_ja: PAMS: 零次LLMファインチューニングのための事前条件付け活性化メトリクス部分空間
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）のファインチューニングにおいて、勾配計算を不要とする零次最適化手法の効率性と安定性を向上させるフレームワーク「PAMS」を提案する。本手法は、前向きパスの活性化統計量を用いて層ごとの構造化された摂動幾何学を構築し、低ランク近似によって計算コストとメモリ使用量を大幅に削減する。理論的には、この摂動共分散がガウス平滑化された目的関数の勾配に対して右側事前条件付けを行うことを示し、非凸収束保証を導出している。GLUEおよびSuperGLUEタスクでの実験により、勾配ベース手法に匹敵する性能と安定性を、勾配計算なしで実現できることを実証した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの効率化・推論高速化・ファインチューニング手法に直結する高関連論文

papers.title: DisSparse: Pipelined Top-$p$ Sparse Attention for Long-Context LLM Serving
papers.summary: Long-context LLM inference is bottlenecked by the memory demands of the key-value (KV) cache, whose size scales linearly with context length. Dynamic sparse attention reduces this bottleneck by fetching and attending only to a critical subset of tokens. The dominant primitive in dynamic sparse attention research and deployment is fixed-budget top-$k$ selection, which is favored because its deterministic block count aligns with the static memory allocation that systems like vLLM rely on. Top-$k$ uses a fixed budget regardless of how attention mass is distributed across heads, layers, and decode steps, leading to either wasted bandwidth on heads with peaky attention or dropped context on heads with diffuse attention. Top-$p$ (nucleus) selection adapts naturally to this variation but has seen limited adoption in production serving systems due to two system-level challenges: variable block counts that break deterministic block allocation and computationally expensive selection kernels that exceed the cost of attention itself. We present DisSparse, a serving system that integrates top-$p$ sparse attention into vLLM end-to-end. DisSparse decouples block selection from the scheduler's critical path, hides selection latency behind layer computation via a two-stream pipeline, and introduces a single-pass histogram-based top-$p$ kernel. We further observe intra-block sparsity, the inflation of selection budgets caused by mixing high- and low-importance tokens within fixed-size KV cache blocks, and address it with a token relocation kernel guided by accumulated prefill attention scores. Across long- and medium-context benchmarks on multiple models, DisSparse achieves 1.17x to 1.80x speedup in sparsity analysis (block selection) over state-of-the-art top-$p$ methods with negligible accuracy loss and supports up to 8x larger maximum batch sizes than dense vLLM under the same memory budget.
papers.title_ja: DisSparse: 長文脈LLMサービングのためのパイプライン型Top-pスパースアテンション
papers.summary_ja: 長文脈LLM推論におけるKVキャッシュのメモリボトルネックを解決するため、動的スパースアテンション手法であるTop-p選択をvLLMに統合したサービングシステムDisSparseを提案する。従来の固定予算Top-kとは異なり、アテンション分布に応じてブロック数を適応させることで、帯域幅の無駄やコンテキスト欠落を回避する。ブロック選択をスケジューラのクリティカルパスから分離し、2ストリームパイプラインとヒストグラムベースの高速カーネルにより選択遅延を隠蔽する。さらに、ブロック内のトークン重要度分布に基づいた再配置カーネルを導入し、既存手法比1.17〜1.80倍の高速化と、同等メモリ条件下で最大8倍のバッチサイズ向上を実現した。

papers.title: BitShare: Sensitivity-Aware Binning and Bit Sharing for Compacting LLM Weight Storage
papers.summary: Decoding with large language models at small batch sizes is limited by memory bandwidth, so the bits stored per weight largely set its cost. Group-wise integer quantization stores every weight of a group at the same precision, although the input channels of a group differ in sensitivity. We present BITSHARE, a codebook-free weight format that keeps the integer grid and the dequantizer of group-wise quantization but varies precision within each group. Sensitivity-aware binning places the channels of each group into three bins at fixed positions, and static bit sharing with optimal bit-value allocation lets the less sensitive weights share their lower bits, each stored once per group or once per pair of weights. A sharing-aware version of GPTQ chooses every stored value, with no fine-tuning and no codebook. BITSHARE has two modes. BITSHARE-U gives every group the same layout, so its decoder routes bits by fixed wiring, while BITSHARE-N chooses a layout per group within the same bit budget. With calibration on the Pile and at the same storage, both modes have lower perplexity than GPTQ at 3 and 2 bits on WikiText-2 and C4. At 2 bits across Llama-2 and Llama-3 models, BITSHARE-N lowers WikiText-2 perplexity by up to 70% against SliM-LLM and up to 35% against GPTAQ. At the 2-bit perplexity of SliM-LLM, BITSHARE-U stores 13.6-19.4% fewer bits per weight, cutting DRAM weight traffic by the same fraction. A verified hardware decoder implementation synthesized in SkyWater 130 nm reconstructs BITSHARE weights at the throughput of INT-n and SliM-LLM decoders.
papers.title_ja: BitShare: LLMの重みストレージ圧縮のための感度認識型バインニングとビット共有
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）のデコーディングにおけるメモリ帯域幅の制約を緩和するため、グループ内での重みの感度差を活かした新しい量子化手法「BITSHARE」を提案する。感度認識型バインニングによりグループ内のチャネルを3つのビンに分類し、低感度の重みは下位ビットを共有することで、コードブックやファインチューニングなしで効率的な重み保存を実現する。GPTQやSliM-LLMと比較し、2ビット量子化においてWikiText-2のパープレキシティを最大70%低減し、同等の品質で13.6〜19.4%のビット数削減とDRAMトラフィックの低減を達成した。さらに、SkyWater 130nmプロセスで検証されたハードウェアデコーダにより、既存のINT-nやSliM-LLMデコーダと同等のスループットでの復元が可能であることを示した。

papers.title: Feedback Shortcut: Speculative Decoding for Latent Feedback Transformers
papers.summary: Feeding each position's top-layer hidden state back into the next position's input improves Transformer performance. However, this feedback breaks speculative decoding, since verifying a drafted token requires the top-layer state from its preceding position, which forces the draft to rely on an approximate stand-in. Training the model to adapt to this stand-in can lower the exact-decoding performance ceiling, while using it at inference time further introduces approximation error. We propose Feedback Shortcut to address both bottlenecks. First, state alignment trains a lightweight projection from multi-token prediction head states to stand-ins, leaving base model training untouched. Second, pipelined correction re-evaluates each draft using its predecessor's newly computed state, a much closer proxy to true feedback. Running this correction inside the verification pass of subsequent drafts improves accuracy with zero extra calls. Across 135M and 780M scales, Feedback Shortcut stays within $10^{-4}$ bits per byte of the exact-decoding ceiling on Paloma and accelerates decoding by 2.4-2.8x with about 2% more training compute than the latent feedback Transformer. At large batch sizes, skipping correction still preserves Transformer speed and over 80% of latent feedback's gains.
papers.title_ja: フィードバックショートカット：潜在フィードバックTransformerのための投機的デコーディング
papers.summary_ja: 潜在フィードバックTransformerにおける投機的デコーディングの阻害要因を解決する手法を提案する。マルチトークン予測ヘッドの状態からスタンドインへの変換を学習し、パイプライン補正により精度と速度を両立させる。135M〜780M規模のモデルで、厳密デコーディングの上限に極めて近い精度を維持しつつ、2.4〜2.8倍の高速化を実現した。

papers.title: SatMend: LLM Agents for Automated Software Repair in Satellite Constellations with Intermittent Ground Contact
papers.summary: Satellite constellations rely on onboard software to sustain services across cooperating spacecraft. Maintaining this software requires handling related component versions and different failure causes while delivering repairs through intermittent ground contact. Automated software repair in satellite constellations remains underexplored, particularly the coordination of repairs across related versions with verified onboard recovery under intermittent ground contact. To address this gap, we propose SatMend, a software repair method driven by ground-based large language model (LLM) agents. SatMend organizes related versions into persistent sessions to retain diagnostic context and combines source and runtime evidence to select code repair or state recovery actions. It validates each version separately and submits ready candidates during continued repair, allowing ground preparation to overlap with onboard delivery and verification. Experimental results show that across configurations with 16 to 64 satellites, SatMend restores 192 of 224 faulty applications within 600 s, compared with 40 for SWE-agent, 77 for Agentless, 124 for RepairAgent, and 115 for SWE-Search. These results demonstrate SatMend's effectiveness in restoring applications and supporting service continuity in satellite constellations with intermittent ground contact.
papers.title_ja: SatMend: 地上との断続的通信下における衛星コンステレーション向け自動ソフトウェア修復のためのLLMエージェント
papers.summary_ja: 地上との通信が断続的な衛星コンステレーションにおいて、LLMエージェントを用いた自動ソフトウェア修復手法「SatMend」を提案する。関連するバージョンを永続セッションとして管理し、ソースコードと実行時証拠を組み合わせて修復アクションを選択する。各バージョンの検証を個別に行いながら、地上での準備と機上での配信・検証を並行処理することで効率を向上させる。実験では、16〜64基の衛星構成で224件の障害のうち192件を600秒以内に復旧し、既存のエージェント手法（SWE-agent等）を大幅に上回る性能を示した。

papers.title: Constraining Planet Nine with Pulsar Timing: Orbit Determination Method from the Acceleration, Jerk, and Snap of the Solar System Barycenter
papers.summary: Planet Nine is hypothesized to exist in the outer solar system in order to explain the physical orbital clustering of several trans-Neptunian objects. A Planet Nine would systematically change the location of the solar system barycenter (SSB). Therefore, the precise timing properties of millisecond radio pulsars would measure the acceleration, jerk, and snap of the currently-perceived SSB under the gravitational influence of a Planet Nine. We present a method on how to use pulsar spin frequency derivatives and binary pulsar orbital period derivatives to constrain the Planet Nine parameter space. We find that searches for unidentified massive objects in the solar system require at least cubic and quartic variations in the pulse times of arrival (corresponding to jerk and snap, respectively) in order to uniquely constrain an orbit. Otherwise, additional assumptions are required to fully constrain the mass and orbital parameters of the object. We use our method to weigh the ice giants Uranus and Neptune and obtain results consistent with the literature. This method could be used to weigh a Planet Nine after a putative optical detection. Future work will use updated pulsar timing datasets that benefit from longer observational baselines and advances in statistical modeling and noise characterization.
papers.title_ja: パルサータイミングによる第9惑星の制約：太陽系重心の加速度、ジャーク、スナップからの軌道決定手法
papers.summary_ja: 太陽系重心の運動変化（加速度、ジャーク、スナップ）をミリ秒パルサーの精密タイミングで観測し、仮説上の第9惑星の軌道を制約する手法を提案する。パルス到着時刻の3次および4次変化（ジャークとスナップ）を用いることで、質量と軌道要素を一意に決定できることを示した。天王星・海王星への適用で既存文献と整合する結果を得て、将来の光学検出後の質量測定に応用可能であることを確認した。
papers.relevance_reason: 軌道力学・軌道決定・高精度観測データ解析の手法が関心に直結

papers.title: Lifted Multiple Shooting for Parallel-in-Time Contact-Rich Trajectory Optimization
papers.summary: Planning through contact requires accounting for the coupled dynamics of a robot and its environment, including inertial effects, contact forces, and friction. However, the non-smoothness and multimodality of contact dynamics and contact geometry makes gradient-based optimization challenging. In this work, we propose lifted multiple shooting, a trajectory optimization transcription that can be solved directly using nonlinear program solvers. By introducing contact impulses as optimization variables, our formulation allows the optimizer to satisfy the state-transition constraints using friction-cone-feasible impulses while separately enforcing their consistency with the contact model. Our formulation supports a broad class of contact constitutive relations, with sensitivities computed through implicit differentiation. To enable efficient planning over long horizons and for high-dimensional systems, we further introduce IP-PAS, a parallel-in-time primal-dual interior-point solver that achieves O(log T) parallel computational depth. We evaluate the proposed methods on six fully dynamic contact-rich planning tasks, including nonprehensile pushing and in-hand manipulation, without contact-guiding costs. Lifted multiple shooting improves success rates by up to 81.5 percentage points over standard multiple shooting, while IP-PAS achieves solution quality comparable to serial methods with up to a 3.1x speedup and scales to horizons of 40,000 timesteps.
papers.title_ja: 接触が頻繁に発生する軌道最適化のための並列時間方向リフトアップ・マルチシューティング
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、接触力学を伴うロボットの軌道最適化手法「リフトアップ・マルチシューティング」を提案する。接触インパルスを変数として導入することで、非滑らかな接触制約を非線形計画問題として直接解けるように定式化し、暗黙微分により感度計算を行う。さらに、時間方向に並列化可能な primal-dual interior-point ソルバ「IP-PAS」を設計し、計算深度を O(log T) に削減した。6つの動的な接触タスクにおいて、標準手法比で成功率を最大81.5ポイント向上させ、40,000ステップの長いホライズンでも最大3.1倍の高速化を実現した。
papers.relevance_reason: 軌道最適化の高速化と並列計算手法が関心に合致

papers.title: Analysis of the Cosmos 2612 - ICEYE-X36 rendezvous and proximity operation from public orbital element data
papers.summary: We analyse the October 2026 close approach between Cosmos 2612 (NORAD 68762) and the commercial radar satellite ICEYE-X36 (NORAD 59103), both in sun-synchronous low Earth orbit, to determine whether it was a rendezvous and proximity operation (RPO) or the result of natural orbital evolution. The public general perturbations (GP) element history from April to October 2026 was propagated with SGP4, and the prediction error was measured empirically for each object. The null hypothesis of natural evolution, tested with manoeuvre-free propagations, is rejected for all 18 parameter combinations: the encounter required manoeuvres by Cosmos 2612, whereas those of ICEYE-X36 are not needed to reproduce it. Closest approach occurred on 18 October at 06:33 UTC, below 0.79 km (95th percentile), with a local relative velocity of about 0.08 m/s and 41.4 h continuously within 5 km. It was the final stage of a sequence that began in May with a plane match, followed by a phasing drift, the approach and a manoeuvred retreat, with a minimum cumulative $\Delta v$ of 174-180 m/s. The data cannot resolve the minimum distance below their accuracy, nor establish whether the operation was cooperative or its purpose.
papers.title_ja: 公開軌道要素データを用いた Cosmos 2612 と ICEYE-X36 の接近・近接操作の分析
papers.summary_ja: 太陽同期低軌道上の Cosmos 2612 と ICEYE-X36 の接近事象について、公開軌道要素データと SGP4 伝播を用いて自然進化か意図的な接近か判別した。結果、Cosmos 2612 による機動が必須であり、5 月から始まる面一致、位相調整、接近、離脱の一連の操作であったことが示された。最小接近距離は 0.79 km 未満、相対速度は約 0.08 m/s であり、累積 Δv は 174-180 m/s と推定される。ただし、データ精度の限界から最小距離の正確な値や操作の目的（協調的か否か）は特定できなかった。

papers.title: Language Model Harnesses can be Compositional Generalizers
papers.summary: Modern language models (LMs) are post-trained and deployed as agents inside a "harness", but standard harness designs accumulate context that the neural network is forced to generalize to, making training for long-horizon tasks expensive and time-consuming. We study an alternative emerging path: training inherently neurosymbolic LM harnesses, which externalize and manage context programmatically to compose existing LM capabilities. We hypothesize that training around these harnesses can offer a better return on compute by enabling compositional generalization, as they can learn to decompose complex problems so that every observation their neural LM receives is locally in-distribution, even when the full task is novel. We find that harnesses like the Recursive Language Model (RLM) learn such decompositions readily under reinforcement learning post-training: (1) we demonstrate that training only on short tasks can generalize to tasks 2-64$\times$ longer while the base neural LM improves less, and (2) training on one domain transfers to novel domains that share latent structure. On messier, complex tasks, we find that we can target individual LLM calls within a harness by generating and training on easier, synthetically generated surrogate environments with fake tool / sub-calls, a technique we call surrogate harness training. From this finding, we train RLM-27B on synthetic data, and show it improves Qwen3.8-27B in the same RLM harness on a hard suite of long-context tasks like CTC-Bench and ExpertLongBench by 26.9% on average while using $\sim$2$\times$ fewer tokens at inference time. Finally, we show that harnesses can compose over these newly learned decompositions using recursive sub-harness calls.
papers.title_ja: 言語モデルハーネスは構成的汎化器となり得る
papers.summary_ja: 本研究は、コンテキストをプログラム的に管理するニューロシンボリックなLMハーネス（RLM）の強化学習による訓練が、計算効率と構成的汎化能力を向上させることを示す。短いタスクでのみ訓練しても2〜64倍長いタスクに汎化し、異なるドメイン間でも潜在構造を共有すれば転移学習が有効であることが確認された。さらに、合成サロゲート環境を用いた「サロゲートハーネス訓練」により、長文脈タスクでの性能を26.9%向上させつつ推論トークン数を約2倍削減した。

papers.title: Failure Modes and Data-Efficient Remedies for Transformer-Based Prediction of Viscoplastic Flows
papers.summary: Fast and accurate prediction of viscoplastic flows remains a challenge in computational rheology due to yield surfaces, discontinuous gradients, and strongly nonlinear transitions between yielded and unyielded regions. Transformer-based neural operators such as RheOFormer have recently shown strong potential for surrogate modeling of non-Newtonian flows. However, their applicability to viscoplastic systems and their efficacy in recovering realistic flows remain poorly understood. In this work, we present the first systematic investigation of RheOFormer applied to steady Bingham channel flow. By isolating the problem to a simple geometry and constitutive model, we examine how dataset structure, numerical value range, and input representation govern the model's ability to interpolate and extrapolate within the parameter space. The data regimes in which RheOFormer remains accurate and those in which errors emerge are identified, particularly for plug-dominated flows and for conditions outside the velocity scales or flow structures represented during training. Upon identifying these failure modes, targeted enhancements to the input representation and loss formulation are introduced to better predict low-gradient plug regions. Logarithmic velocity representations and gradient-aware loss formulations substantially improve accuracy in challenging regimes where the baseline formulation fails. In addition, extrapolation errors are reduced by augmenting the training set with only a few strategically selected cases spanning the missing physical regimes. Finally, a single partially developed snapshot suffices for an accurate steady-state prediction, and the model outperforms simply copying its input throughout flow development. These results highlight the importance of appropriate field representation and parameter-space coverage for data-efficient neural-operator prediction of viscoplastic flows.
papers.title_ja: 粘塑性流れのTransformerベース予測における失敗モードとデータ効率の良い改善策
papers.summary_ja: 粘塑性流れのサロゲートモデルとしてTransformer型ニューラルオペレータ（RheOFormer）を適用し、その失敗モードを体系的に調査した。データ構造や入力表現が補間・外挿精度に与える影響を分析し、特にプラグ支配領域や訓練範囲外での誤差要因を特定した。対数速度表現や勾配認識型損失関数の導入、および戦略的な少数ケースによる訓練セット拡張により、困難な領域での精度を大幅に向上させた。これらの手法により、データ効率の良い粘塑性流れ予測が可能になった。

papers.title: Finite-difference neural policy iteration for high-dimensional degenerate Hamilton--Jacobi equations
papers.summary: We develop a finite-difference neural policy iteration method for high-dimensional degenerate Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman and Isaacs equations. Artificial viscosity yields a monotone finite-difference operator, and neural networks approximate the linear equations of semi-discrete policy iteration using local stencil values. This avoids global tensor-grid storage. For measurable feedbacks, we bound the propagation of evaluation, terminal, gradient, and control optimization errors by a geometrically weighted sum. Discrete comparison, consistency, and vanishing viscosity relate the approximation to the original degenerate equation. On coupled manufactured problems with rank-deficient diffusion, the method achieves lower mean errors than direct physics-informed neural networks at every tested dimension from five to fifty under equal training time. At fifty dimensions and $900$ seconds, the mean relative $L^2$ error over three paired seeds is about $40\%$ lower. Two-dimensional refinement attains $0.297\%$ error against the original degenerate solution, with independent grid references separating approximation error from viscosity bias. In a twenty-dimensional game with finite control sets, reusing policies reduces the measured time to a relative error of $5\%$ by $24.3\%$ compared with direct minimization of the same discrete residual with fresh samples at every update.
papers.title_ja: 高次元退化ハミルトン・ジャコビ方程式のための有限差分ニューラルポリシー反復法
papers.summary_ja: 高次元の退化ハミルトン・ジャコビ・ベルマン方程式を解くための有限差分ニューラルポリシー反復法を提案する。人工粘性を用いた単調な有限差分演算子と、局所ステンシル値によるニューラルネットワーク近似により、グローバルなテンソルグリッドのメモリコストを回避する。5次元から50次元までの製造問題において、同等の訓練時間内で物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）よりも低い平均誤差を達成した。また、20次元のゲーム問題では、ポリシーの再利用により直接最小化法と比較して計算時間を24.3%短縮しつつ、5%の相対誤差を達成した。
papers.relevance_reason: 高次元PDE解法とPINN比較、最適化手法の効率化が関心に合致

papers.title: Random Projection Neural Networks for Phase-Field Models: Model Reformulation, Scaling, and Network Architecture
papers.summary: Phase-field models, particularly the Allen-Cahn(AC) and Cahn-Hilliard(CH) equations, are widely used to describe interfacial dynamics, but resolving their sharp transition layers and stiff dynamics presents substantial numerical challenges. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) offer a mesh-free approach, yet optimizing large numbers of network parameters can be computationally demanding and may still yield limited accuracy. We develop a random projection neural network (RPNN) framework that combines first-order PDE reformulations with independent random-feature representations of the unknowns. By fixing randomly initialized hidden-layer parameters and optimizing only the output coefficients, RPNNs reduce training to least-squares problems amenable to Newton-type solvers. Introducing auxiliary variables eliminates higher-order derivatives from the PDE residuals, while separate random feature bases in the unknowns provide flexibility in approximating fields with different scales and regularity. For the CH equation, we scale the chemical potential to address the disparity between its magnitude and that of the phase field. We compare the first-order and corresponding higher-order formulations and systematically examine the effects of initialization distributions, the random feature range $R_\xi$, seven activation functions, and dense versus separable space-time bases. We also evaluate gradient-based adaptive sampling, residual reweighting, and mild spatial derivative-penalty regularization. Across the reported benchmarks, the proposed framework reduces relative $L^2$ and absolute $L^\infty$ errors by nearly one to three orders of magnitude compared with the various PINN baselines. These results demonstrate the potential of first-order RPNNs for accurate approximation of phase-field dynamics with sharp transition layers.
papers.title_ja: 相場モデルのためのランダム射影ニューラルネットワーク：モデル再定式化、スケーリング、およびネットワークアーキテクチャ
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、Allen-CahnおよびCahn-Hilliard方程式などの相場モデルを解くためのランダム射影ニューラルネットワーク（RPNN）フレームワークを提案する。未知数を独立したランダム特徴量で表現し、隠れ層パラメータを固定することで、最適化をニュートン法適用可能な最小二乗問題に削減する。さらに、高次微分を排除する一次PDE再定式化や、化学ポテンシャルのスケーリングを導入し、PINNベースラインと比較して相対L2誤差および絶対L∞誤差を1〜3桁低減する精度を達成した。

papers.title: RSLaA: Self-Reconfiguring Roadside LiDARs as Agents for 3D Traffic Perception
papers.summary: Cooperative perception with roadside LiDARs (RSLs) extends the sensing range of autonomous vehicles and resolves onboard-sensor occlusions, particularly at curves and intersections. Because infrastructure deployment is costly, existing work optimizes RSL configurations once, against road geometry and aggregated traffic statistics, and treats them as fixed thereafter. Traffic flow, however, is inherently dynamic, and a placement optimal on average can be far from optimal at any given moment. We introduce RSLaA (Roadside LiDARs as Agents), a framework in which each RSL adaptively adjusts its pose to the evolving traffic scene over decision-time windows. Since ground truth is unavailable at decision time, the framework centers on surrogate metrics computed solely from a probabilistic occupancy grid of historical observations, which predicts the next-window perception performance of candidate poses. We construct a co-simulation benchmark pairing five candidate surrogates with detector-agnostic ground-truth perception labels at every decision window, identifying the multi-view coverage metric J_mv as the most reliable predictor. Upon this validated surrogate we build two adaptive configuration methods, a receding-horizon (MPC) optimizer and a lightweight MAPPO-based multi-agent reinforcement learning scheme with centralized training and decentralized execution. Across 10 sites and 89 six-hour traffic scenarios (890 evaluation runs), adaptive configuration consistently improves the composite perception score over static deployment. Our results indicate that RSLs could be benefitted from being treated as agents.
papers.title_ja: RSLaA: 3D交通認識のための自己再構成型路側LiDARエージェント
papers.summary_ja: 路側LiDAR（RSL）の配置を固定ではなく、交通状況に応じて動的に調整するフレームワーク「RSLaA」を提案する。決定時に正解データが利用できないため、過去の観測に基づく確率的占有グリッドから計算されるサロゲート指標を用いて、次ウィンドウの認識性能を予測する手法を採用した。検証されたサロゲート指標に基づき、MPC最適化とMAPPOベースの強化学習による2つの適応型配置手法を構築した。10地点・89シナリオでの評価により、静的配置と比較して認識スコアが向上することが示された。

papers.title: Hybrid state-space and attention neural operators for nonlinear structural dynamics under environmental loading
papers.summary: The computational burden of repeated nonlinear time-history analyses limits their application for structural assessment and design. We therefore propose DeepOJamba, a hybrid neural operator that combines selective state-space recurrence with full attention to predict the structural response history due to dynamic loading. Physical-parameter conditioning and predicted-state transfer between sequences enable a single trained operator to represent varying system conditions and generate response histories beyond its training sequence length. DeepOJamba is evaluated on a 15~MW monopile offshore wind turbine under wind and wave loading. The proposed operator is compared to pure attention, pure state-space, Fourier, and DeepONet operators and is found to give the lowest window error on every channel and the lowest closed-loop fatigue and ultimate-load errors of $9.4\%$ and $6.0\%$, against $14.6\%$ and $8.7\%$ for the next-best pure attention operator examined. Moreover, on sea states outside the training wave band, the error slightly increases by approximately $0.4$ percentage points. Pure state-space operators can approach similar low errors only with a much wider convolution kernel tuned to the tower eigenperiod, which increases the training cost by $40\%$. In all, the results obtained support hybrid neural operators for robust long-duration structural response and demand prediction.
papers.title_ja: 環境荷重下における非線形構造力学のためのハイブリッド状態空間・アテンションニューラルオペレータ
papers.summary_ja: 非線形構造力学の時間履歴解析における計算負荷を軽減するため、選択的状態空間再帰とフルアテンションを組み合わせるハイブリッドニューラルオペレータ「DeepOJamba」を提案する。物理パラメータの条件付けと予測状態の転送により、異なるシステム条件や訓練長を超える応答履歴の予測を単一モデルで実現する。15MW単脚型洋上風力発電機を対象とした評価では、純粋なアテンションや状態空間モデルと比較し、疲労・極限荷重誤差が最小となり、汎化性能の優位性を示した。

papers.title: World Models Are the Right Foundation for Simulating Mars Terraforming
papers.summary: Terraforming Mars is a long-horizon, action-conditioned control problem that requires predicting atmospheric responses to interventions over centuries to identify effective policies. This position paper argues that physics-regularized recurrent state-space world models are the most promising foundation for this setting. Data-driven climate emulators lack action-conditioning, and physics-based general circulation models (GCMs) are too expensive for policy search. Among learned world models, recurrent state-space architectures with physics constraints are better suited than transformer-based alternatives: they provide native uncertainty quantification through their stochastic-deterministic decomposition, remain stable under sparse non-terrestrial training data, and enforce physical consistency at each rollout step. To make this position concrete, we describe a potential architecture combining JEPA-inspired latent encoding, universal differential equation constraints, and a Dreamer-lineage planning head. We also introduce MarsWorld, an open benchmark proposal for intervention-conditioned planetary world models, and discuss broader implications and objections.
papers.title_ja: 火星の地球化シミュレーションにおけるワールドモデルの基礎的役割
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、火星の地球化という長期かつ行動条件付きの制御問題に対し、物理則を正規化された再帰型状態空間ワールドモデルが最も有望な基盤であると主張する。データ駆動型気候エミュレータは行動条件付けが不足し、物理ベースの一般循環モデル（GCM）はポリシー探索に高コストであるため、学習型ワールドモデルの中でも再帰型アーキテクチャが適していると論じる。具体的には、JEPAインスパイアの潜在エンコーディング、普遍微分方程式の制約、Dreamer系プランニングヘッドを組み合わせるアーキテクチャを提案する。また、介入条件付き惑星ワールドモデルのためのオープンベンチマーク「MarsWorld」も提唱している。
papers.relevance_reason: 軌道力学・宇宙機設計とML手法（サロゲート・物理情報）の組み合わせに直結

papers.title: Beyond PINNs: Boundary-Enriched Holomorphic Networks for Laplace Problems
papers.summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) solve partial differential equations by penalizing their residual, but this formulation can be difficult to optimize for solutions with singular behaviour. We focus specifically on the two-dimensional Laplace equation, whose strong analytical structure allows the governing equation to be enforced directly in the neural representation. We compare a hybrid harmonic-neural model with a holomorphic neural network whose output is harmonic by construction and therefore requires only boundary training. We further enrich the holomorphic model with singular functions chosen according to the interior angle and boundary conditions at each junction of boundary segments. On six singular benchmarks, the enriched model is the most accurate of the neural models we compare. On the four with a closed-form solution, however, that solution lies in the span of the enrichment terms, and a least-squares fit of these terms alone is exact to rounding error. On Motz's problem and the cracked beam, the neural core reduces the relative error of the recovered leading singular coefficient from about $10^{-2}$, for a least-squares fit with the same four terms, to about $10^{-6}$, and on four variants whose solution has a smooth part outside the span, the network is $4\times10^{4}$ to $2\times10^{7}$ times more accurate than a fit of its singular terms alone; classical least-squares fits with more singular terms, or with harmonic polynomials and rational poles, are more accurate still. Our results demonstrate how exploiting problem-specific analytical structure can provide an alternative to base and residual PINNs for challenging scientific computing problems.
papers.title_ja: PINNsを超えて：ラプラス問題のための境界強化ホロモルフィックネットワーク
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINNs）の最適化困難さを克服するため、2次元ラプラス方程式に特化した新しいアプローチを提案する。出力が構造的に調和関数となるホロモルフィックネットワークを用い、境界条件のみで学習を行うことで残差ペナルティを不要とする。さらに、特異点の角度や境界条件に基づいて選択した特異関数でモデルを強化し、6つのベンチマークで既存のニューラルモデル中最も高い精度を達成した。ただし、閉形式解が存在するケースでは最小二乗法による特異関数のフィッティングがより正確であり、ニューラルコアは滑らかな成分を含む問題で特異係数の復元精度を大幅に向上させることを示した。

papers.title: Topology-Prior-Guided Regional Latent Dynamics for Transient Structural Response Prediction
papers.summary: Predicting the transient nonlinear responses of complex engineering structures remains challenging due to large finite element meshes, heterogeneous structural components, and history-dependent mechanical behavior. This study proposes a topology-prior-guided regional latent dynamics (TPLD) surrogate model that combines physically structured regional representations with dynamics-aware latent learning for full-field time-history prediction. Based on mesh topology and engineering priors, structural responses are encoded into spatially coupled regional latent variables through region-aware feature extraction and topology-constrained interactions. An auxiliary one-step prediction task enhances latent-space dynamical predictability by introducing state-transition supervision. A load-conditioned spatiotemporal Mamba model then predicts regional latent trajectories by integrating temporal causal scanning and bidirectional spatial scanning, while a shared coordinate-conditioned decoder reconstructs full-field nodal responses. The framework is evaluated on three finite element datasets: a parametric stiffened panel, a partitioned pressure impact plate, and a Toyota Yaris full-vehicle crash model. The relative L2 errors for the three displacement components range from 4.00% to 8.21% on the stiffened panel and from 1.41% to 12.22% on the approximately 1.49-million-node vehicle model. On the BIW crash benchmark, TPLD achieves a relative L2 position error of 0.620%, representing a 30.7% reduction compared with the best-performing GeoTransolver configuration. Ablation studies demonstrate the advantages of topology-guided regional representations over global latent and learnable soft-slice alternatives, while auxiliary one-step prediction particularly improves the prediction of accumulated plastic strain.
papers.title_ja: トポロジー事前知識に基づく局所潜在ダイナミクスを用いた一過性構造応答予測
papers.summary_ja: 複雑な工学構造の一過性非線形応答予測を目的とし、メッシュトポロジーと工学的な事前知識を組み合わせたサロゲートモデル「TPLD」を提案する。メッシュ構造に基づき空間的に結合された局所潜在変数へエンコードし、補助的な1ステップ予測タスクにより潜在空間の動的予測可能性を高める。負荷条件付きの時空間Mambaモデルを用いて局所潜在軌道を予測し、共有デコーダで全場の節点応答を再構成する。リジッドパネルやトヨタ・ヤリスの衝突モデルなど3つの有限要素法データセットで評価し、既存手法比で最大30.7%の誤差低減を達成した。

papers.title: IP-GNO: An Inductive Physics-Informed Graph Neural Operator for Automated Distribution System State Estimation
papers.summary: Distribution System State Estimation (DSSE) is a crucial tool for real-time monitoring, operation, and control of the new-age distribution systems (DSs) due to intensified voltage fluctuations and operational uncertainties introduced by volatile power injection at the nodes. Existing GNN-based approaches generally exhibit limited generalization across networks with different sizes and topologies, making zero-shot cross-grid transfer to unseen DSs a significant challenge. To overcome the aforementioned challenges, this article proposes an Inductive Physics-Informed Graph Neural Operator (IP-GNO) for scalable and transferable DSSE. The proposed framework frames complex bus voltage estimation as an operator-learning problem inspired by the Neumann series expansion of the inverse bus admittance matrix. An admittance-parameterized kernel, incorporating a self-admittance gate in the zeroth-order term and a persistent source-injection skip connection across network layers, captures the underlying electrical dependencies. Additionally, a Physics-Embedded Tree Encoding (PETE) scheme introduces five grid-size-invariant positional features derived from path impedance and a DC-linearized phase-angle prior. A sine-cosine output formulation is further employed to address phase-angle periodicity and ensure stable training. The proposed IP-GNO module is evaluated on two small (IEEE 33- and 69-bus), two medium (IEEE 123- and 136-bus), and one large (2522-bus) sized DSs. Particularly, its zero-shot cross-grid generalization capability is investigated by training the model exclusively on the IEEE 33-bus system and directly evaluating it on four unseen distribution networks of different sizes without retraining or fine-tuning. A detailed comparative analysis with the existing state-of-the-art DSSE tools proves the superiority of IP-GNO, enabling scalable DSSE across heterogeneous DSs.
papers.title_ja: IP-GNO: 自動配電システム状態推定のための帰納的・物理情報グラフニューラルオペレータ
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、配電システムにおける電圧推定（DSSE）の汎化性能を高めるために、物理情報グラフニューラルオペレータ（IP-GNO）を提案する。ニューマン級数展開に着想を得た演算子学習の枠組みを用い、インピーダンスや位相角の物理的制約をエンコードすることで、異なる規模やトポロジーのネットワーク間でのゼロショット転移を可能にする。IEEE 33バスで訓練したモデルを、最大2522バスの未知のネットワークに適用し、既存手法を上回る推定精度とスケーラビリティを実証した。

papers.title: Flood forecasting using a physics-guided conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model
papers.summary: High-resolution flood forecasting with full two-dimensional shallow water equation (SWE) solvers remains computationally expensive, even on GPUs. We develop a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) that forecasts the evolution of 30 m water-depth fields over a four-day horizon for the Des Plaines River watershed, Illinois. The model is trained on SynxFlow SWE simulations of 113 historical storms observed across twelve Midwestern states (2003-2024), each under three antecedent-wetness scenarios, and can optionally be conditioned on coarse 100 m or 150 m hydrodynamic simulations. Because reverse diffusion is stochastic, every forecast is a 20-member ensemble drawn from the same trained model. Coarse conditioning reduces the four-day mean water-depth RMSE of the ensemble mean from 0.170 m to 0.054 m (100 m) and 0.048 m (150 m). The coarser 150 m conditioning also gives the best critical success index (0.839), false alarm ratio, CRPS and Brier score at lower cost, so finer conditioning does not guarantee better skill. Averaging members reduces error by 5-11% relative to a single realization, and the ensemble provides spatially explicit exceedance probabilities, although the ensembles are under-dispersive (spread-to-error ratios 0.35-0.73). On a single GPU, a four-day forecast over 26 non-overlapping patches is 7.8x, 11.0x and 16.3x faster than the 30 m simulation for the 100 m, 150 m and unconditioned configurations, and projected speedups for a 14-day forecast reach 12-49x for one member and 48-58x for 20 members. Physics-guided diffusion models are thus promising probabilistic surrogates for regional-scale flood forecasting.
papers.title_ja: 物理情報付き条件付きデノイジング拡散確率モデルを用いた洪水予測

papers.title: Multi-Order Passive Macromodeling from Layouts via Nested Port-Hamiltonian Learning
papers.summary: Compact, passive state-space macromodels of interconnects and power-delivery networks are essential for stable transient signal- and power-integrity simulations. However, conventional flows require costly per-layout full-wave electromagnetic (EM) simulations, while both traditional fitting and prior learning surrogates rely on post-hoc fitting or passivity perturbation that degrades accuracy without guaranteeing convergence. In this work, we propose an end-to-end macromodeling framework that learns directly in the passive space, mapping physical layout graphs to multi-order port-Hamiltonian (pH) macromodels. Specifically, our network encodes each layout graph into unconstrained matrix blocks and assembles them via a complete, prefix-nested pH parameterization that guarantees continuous-frequency passivity and stability by construction, yielding valid $k$-state macromodels via direct state slicing in one forward pass. To train all orders without reference realizations, we supervise the network directly on S-parameters through a progressive order-growth curriculum. Evaluated on 27k unseen test structures from a 270k-structure advanced-packaging dataset, our framework reduces mean S-parameter error by $42\%$ on average (up to $65\%$) over established macromodeling tools fitted to ground-truth EM responses, achieves zero passivity violations across $459{,}000$ exported models, and accelerates macromodel generation by $11{,}000$--$39{,}000\times$ ($36$--$85$~ms per layout).
papers.title_ja: ネスト型ポート・ハミルトニアン学習によるレイアウトからの多次数パッシブマクロモデリング
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、ICLや電力配給ネットワークの安定したシミュレーションに必要なパッシブな状態空間マクロモデルを、物理レイアウトグラフから直接学習するエンドツーエンドフレームワークを提案する。従来の事後フィッティングやパッシビティ補正に頼らず、ポート・ハミルトニアン（pH）パラメータ化を用いることで、連続周波数でのパッシビティと安定性を構造的に保証する。Sパラメータを直接教師信号とする段階的学習により、参照実装なしで多次数モデルを生成し、27万構造のデータセットで既存ツール比42%の誤差低減と1万倍以上の高速化を実現した。

papers.title: Correlation-aware sequential sampling for multi-output polynomial chaos expansions
papers.summary: The interaction of multiple physical processes in complex engineering systems is often characterized by several quantities of interest (QoIs) with non-negligible cross-correlations. Accurate uncertainty quantification of these responses requires repeated model evaluations, which can be computationally expensive. As an alternative, polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) provides an efficient surrogate modeling framework for reducing this computational cost owing to its natural structure for statistical analysis, while adaptive sequential sampling can further improve sampling efficiency under a limited model evaluation budget. However, adaptive sampling strategies specifically designed for multi-output PCE remain limited, and existing approaches commonly aggregate information from individual outputs without explicitly accounting for their statistical dependence. When strong correlations exist among QoIs, output-wise aggregation can give greater combined influence to response patterns shared by several outputs. To reduce the influence of such repeated representation on sample allocation, this study develops a principal component analysis-based extension of the multi-output criterion for adaptive construction of PCE. The sampling criterion combines component-wise normalization with the retention of selected principal directions, thereby adjusting the relative influence of shared response patterns while preserving distance-based exploration. The method is verified through numerical examples with different levels of output coupling and is compared with the conventional multi-output criterion and reference sampling strategies. The results demonstrate that accounting for output dependence improves the allocation of new samples among multiple response features and enhances the efficiency of multi-output PCE surrogate construction, particularly for strongly correlated QoIs.
papers.title_ja: 多出力多項式カオス展開のための相関考慮型逐次サンプリング
papers.summary_ja: 複雑な工学系における複数の関心量（QoI）間の相関を考慮し、多項式カオス展開（PCE）によるサロゲートモデル構築の効率を高める手法を提案する。既存の適応サンプリングが出力間の統計的依存性を無視しがちである問題に対し、主成分分析（PCA）を用いて基準を拡張した。これにより、共有される応答パターンへの過剰なサンプル割当を抑制しつつ、探索性を維持する。数値例により、特に強い相関を持つQoIにおいて、従来の手法よりサンプル配分が改善され、サロゲート構築の効率が向上することを示した。

papers.title: Watermark Claims Under Test: Lessons from Auditing a Production LLM
papers.summary: Can we tell whether an LLM is watermarked without knowing its secret key? Published black-box tests suggest that carefully designed prompts can reveal the statistical footprint of a watermark. This paper examines what happens when those tests move from controlled reference implementations to a deployed model whose watermarking parameters are undisclosed. We present an audit of the Red-Green watermark presence test on Claude. Across ten initial configurations, the published test never rejects on a model the provider states is watermarked, despite detecting a local reference at comparable sample sizes. Controlled experiments expose a failure mode: including the prompt in the watermark's repeated-context history suppresses marking exactly where the test measures it. The watermark remains active, but the probe becomes blind. Attempts to repair the probe reveal further confounds. Constructed contexts can trigger native digit-to-word preferences, while comparisons within a single response can measure how the model plans its answer. Tokenization changes which contexts the probe actually controls. These findings show why validation on a surrogate model does not establish validity on the model under investigation. A redesigned probe finds a substantial context-dependent shift on Claude Fable that is absent on two sibling controls. However, the pre-registered decision remains inconclusive because selective refusals violate the protocol, and the effect's watermark origin is unresolved. We show how to design controls, distinguish statistical rejection from evidence of watermarking and interpret a null without treating it as proof of absence. We provide researchers and practitioners working on LLM evaluation, watermarking, and provenance with an audit checklist grounded in concrete successes and failures. Code, prompts, and parsed responses are available for reproducing the analyses.
papers.title_ja: ウォーターマーク主張の検証：本番環境LLM監査から得た教訓
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、秘密鍵を知らずにLLMのウォーターマーク存在を検出するブラックボックステストの実効性を、Claudeという本番モデルで監査したものである。公開テストは参照実装では機能するが、本番モデルではプロンプトがコンテキスト履歴に含まれることでマーキングが抑制され、検出不能になるという失敗モードを特定した。さらに、トークナイゼーションやモデルの回答計画が検出結果に与える影響を分析し、サロゲートモデルでの検証が対象モデルの妥当性を保証しないことを示した。最終的に再設計したプローブで文脈依存シフトを発見したが、プロトコル違反により結論は不確定であり、LLM評価・ウォーターマーク・プロベナンス研究のための監査チェックリストを提供する。

papers.title: FP-Prune: Rethinking Visual Token Pruning from an Information Gain Perspective
papers.summary: Visual token pruning can reduce the inference cost of vision language models, but its effectiveness depends on preserving complementary visual information under a limited token budget. A central challenge is to quantify the additional information a candidate token contributes beyond the retained set, a contribution that conventional scores based on attention or similarity struggle to capture directly. In this work, we revisit visual token pruning from the perspective of information gain and use mutual information to characterize the incremental value of candidate tokens. We further establish theoretically that frame potential serves as an effective surrogate for mutual information. Building on this observation, we propose FP-Prune, a training-free visual token pruning method that iteratively removes tokens with low information gain to preserve as much complementary visual information as possible. Experiments on three widely used VLMs and eight datasets demonstrate that FP-Prune outperforms baseline methods in both accuracy and inference efficiency. Further analysis shows that the surrogate objective closely aligns with model performance. Our work provides theoretical grounding and an effective method for visual token pruning.
papers.title_ja: FP-Prune: 情報利得の視点から再考する視覚トークン剪定
papers.summary_ja: 視覚言語モデル（VLM）の推論コスト削減を目的とした視覚トークン剪定手法を提案する。従来のアテンションや類似度ベースのスコアでは捉えきれない候補トークンの追加情報量を、相互情報量を用いて定量化する。理論的にフレームポテンシャルが相互情報量の有効なサロゲートであることを示し、これに基づいて学習不要で低情報利得のトークンを反復的に除去するFP-Pruneを設計した。3つのVLMと8つのデータセットでの実験により、精度と推論効率の両面でベースラインを上回ることを実証した。

papers.title: Efficient Optimization of Mechanical Metamaterials via Transferable Representation Learning
papers.summary: Designing mechanical metamaterials for nonlinear behavior such as energy absorption is limited by high-dimensional parametrizations and by expensive simulations. Here we show that design knowledge from a cheap linear property can be transferred to nonlinear, potentially non-differentiable, targets through a learned, reusable search space. TRAMA (TRAnsferable representation learning for Metamaterial Architectures) reparametrizes architected materials using a variational autoencoder with a pre-trained vision transformer and physics-informed augmentations. For energy-absorption efficiency, TRAMA reaches every efficiency level with 95 to 98% reduction in the evaluations needed by state-of-the-art gradient-free optimization and 3 to 5 fewer than gradient-based optimization. Its best design is comparable to the best found by any baseline with at least 67% fewer evaluations, which translate into approximately 100 hours saved per campaign with finite-element simulations. Fabricated designs match simulated stress-strain curves within 5.3%. A post hoc analysis shows where the representation transfers to new properties and where it does not.
papers.title_ja: 転移可能な表現学習による機械メタマテリアルの効率的最適化
papers.summary_ja: 機械メタマテリアルの設計において、高次元パラメータ空間と高コストなシミュレーションを課題とする問題を解決する手法TRAMAを提案する。事前学習済みビジョントランスフォーマーと物理情報拡張を用いた変分オートエンコーダで設計空間を再パラメータ化し、線形特性から非線形特性への知識転移を実現する。エネルギー吸収効率の最適化において、既存手法比で評価回数を95〜98%削減し、有限要素法シミュレーションによる計算時間を大幅に短縮した。製造した試料の応力-ひずみ曲線はシミュレーション結果と5.3%以内の一致を示し、実務的な有効性を検証した。

papers.title: Measuring and Teaching Language Model Agents to Act on Delayed Consequences
papers.summary: Language model agents are increasingly asked to run ongoing multi-day operations rather than finish isolated single-turn tasks. In daily operations, today's choices reshape later observations and cash constraints because empty shelves hide lost walk-in demand, short-shipped customers quietly shrink future orders weeks later, and emergency buying drains working capital. We introduce SMB Bench, a calibrated 90-day wholesale simulator with 18 causally paired tasks and an 859-run frontier trace dataset, to ask what experience and learning signal make an agent better at noticing, attributing, and acting on the delayed consequences of its own decisions in unseen businesses. Across 16 frontier models, only 3 outperform a fixed buying rule; models often record a relevant diagnosis in their notes without changing later purchases in time, showing that diagnosing a problem, changing behavior, and improving a business are separate achievements. To study how experience improves those failures in an open model (Qwen3.8-27B), we used training-business records to identify operational rules and archived frontier quarters as starting states to continue from rather than transcripts to copy. On an unseen test business under identical evaluation instructions, the trained policy followed customer-protection commitments more consistently and reduced severe-loss quarters, while the additional profit benefit remained uncertain. Carrying those commitments through the quarter exposed the cost of fulfilling them, as early-quarter stocking habits left the buyer relying on emergency supply and a deteriorating supplier. The results separate recognizing a delayed effect, acting on it consistently, and coordinating surrounding decisions so that the response improves profit. SMB Bench connects these observations to a learning method by turning archived decisions and their consequences into reusable training experience.
papers.title_ja: 遅延結果に対する行動をLLMエージェントに測定・教育する
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、LLMエージェントが長期的な業務運営において、自身の決定がもたらす遅延結果（例：在庫切れによる将来の需要損失）を認識し、行動に反映できるかを評価するベンチマーク「SMB Bench」を提案する。16のフロンティアモデルを比較した結果、固定ルールを上回るモデルはわずか3つであり、問題の診断と行動変容、事業改善は別々の達成事項であることを示した。さらに、オープンモデル（Qwen3.8-27B）に対し、過去の決定と結果を再利用可能な学習経験として活用する手法を適用し、顧客保護コミットメントの遵守率向上と深刻な損失四半期の削減を確認した。この研究は、エージェントが遅延効果を認識し、一貫して行動し、周囲の決定を調整して利益を改善するプロセスを分離して分析し、実務的なエージェント設計への示唆を与える。

papers.title: AutoPILOT: A Visual Agent Harness for Real-Time Gameplay
papers.summary: Multimodal foundation models can play video games well when the game waits for them, but often fail when it keeps running. We find that much of this gap lies in the harness, which decides what the model sees, what it remembers, and how its outputs become actions over time. Existing harnesses such as VISTA improve the first two, yet turn each model call into at most one action, so the agent acts only as often as its model thinks. We introduce AutoPILOT, which changes the third: in each model call, the model can send a primitive action, start an open-loop macro, or write a closed-loop controller that keeps playing from the screen without further model calls until it hands control back. To evaluate agents in real-time games, we build AFK-Bench, 120 diverse browser games grouped by how they respond to inaction and playable in real time or with the clock paused. With GPT-6.1 Sol under the same budgets, AutoPILOT reaches 68.6% real-time success against 38.3% for VISTA, and on GameWorld it keeps 80.0% in real time while VISTA drops from 84.1% to 42.9%. Its gains hold across models, and it reaches VISTA's final success rate at a fifth of its API cost. Our results suggest that how a harness turns model outputs into actions over time is a central yet underexplored part of agent design, and we hope AutoPILOT and AFK-Bench will serve as a foundation for agents in a world that does not wait.
papers.title_ja: AutoPILOT: リアルタイムゲームプレイのためのビジュアルエージェントハーネス
papers.summary_ja: マルチモーダル基盤モデルがリアルタイムゲームで失敗する原因が、モデル出力をアクションに変換する「ハーネス」設計にあることを指摘する。提案手法AutoPILOTは、モデル呼び出しごとにプリミティブアクション、オープンループマクロ、またはクローズドループコントローラを選択可能にし、モデル推論なしで継続的にプレイできる。新設ベンチマークAFK-Benchを用いた評価では、既存手法VISTA比でリアルタイム成功率を大幅向上させ、APIコストを1/5に削減した。エージェント設計における時間軸上のアクション制御が重要であることを示す。
