papers.title: INSEP: Refusal-Direction Inseparability as a Defense Against Abliteration
papers.summary: Abliteration is a widely used white-box attack against the safety alignment of large language models (LLMs). It elicits harmful behavior by estimating a refusal direction in the model's activation space and projecting that direction out of the residual-stream write-out matrices. We propose INSEP, a defense that fine-tunes the model to reduce the separability of harmful and benign activations along the refusal direction. Abliteration estimates this direction as a difference in class means and projects it out. Reducing separability weakens the signal the attack relies on. An adversarial eigendecomposition selects the most separable prompt subsets. A low-rank adapter reduces their separation along that direction. Behavioral losses preserve the base model's refusal and the quality of its benign responses during training. We benchmark INSEP against six published defenses under five attacks, across eight LLMs from 1B to 14B parameters and several model families. Beyond response harm, we measure coherence, directness, over-refusal, and MMLU, to distinguish robust refusal from low harm produced by evasive or degraded responses. INSEP ranks first on the mean composite score across all eight base models while retaining utility, in the largest abliteration-defense evaluation reported to date.
papers.title_ja: INSEP: 拒否方向の分離不能性を活用したAbliteration攻撃への防御
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）の安全性アライメントに対するホワイトボックス攻撃「Abliteration」への防御手法INSEPを提案する。本手法は、有害なアクティベーションと無害なアクティベーションの拒否方向における分離可能性を低減させることで、攻撃が依存するシグナルを弱める。敵対的固有値分解により最も分離しやすいプロンプトサブセットを選択し、低ランクアダプタを用いてその方向の分離を抑制する。8つのLLMモデルで6つの既存防御手法と比較評価し、有害性だけでなく一貫性や過剰拒否、MMLUスコアも考慮した総合評価で最高成績を収めた。

papers.title: Engram: Multi-Stage Memory for Agentic Tuning of Heterogeneous Models
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents can now tune neural networks, yet without cross-session memory they spend costly trials rediscovering known lessons. Reuse is difficult because production models differ in architecture, training setup and inference budget. We present Engram, a memory system that links past trial outcomes with the hypotheses and rationale behind them and assesses whether this evidence applies to the current model. An online agent curates evidence at the decision points where it is needed: Initial Guidance supplies validated lessons at the start, Session Retrieval supplies related past sessions before each batch of hypotheses is generated, and Trial Candidate Review checks each trial candidate against matching past trials. Between sessions, an offline agent distills validated lessons, making the memory self-improving. On two ads models, Engram reaches the 32-trial result of a no-memory control with 47% fewer trials and also ends with a better model on average.
papers.title_ja: Engram: 異種モデルのエージェントチューニングのための多段階メモリ

papers.title: When a Permitted Action Completes a Forbidden Workflow: Designing Consequence-Oriented Approval for LLM Agents
papers.summary: Tool-using language-model agents increasingly ask people to approve consequential actions, yet an approval prompt shows only the next step. A request to send a file to an approved recipient can look harmless even when that file was assembled, several steps earlier, from data the user said must never leave. We call this a cumulative authorization failure and argue that it is an interaction design problem as much as a security problem. The evidence a reviewer needs is spread across the trajectory, and listing it in time order leaves the reviewer to reconstruct the causal chain. We present the Cumulative Consent Ledger (CCL), an approval interface built on four design principles that restate the user's intent, bind the review to the exact action, compose the cumulative consequence, and keep every claim checkable. A trusted monitor that tracks artifact lineage supplies the evidence. In a between-subjects study with 80 participants and 960 approval decisions, CCL was associated with fewer unsafe approvals than an evidence-matched chronological log (24.2% vs. 32.5%), higher comprehension, and faster decisions, although the adjusted difference in unsafe approvals remained uncertain (-7.9 points, 95% CrI [-19.7, 3.8]). In a system evaluation, the monitor detected 89.2% of 120 violating checkpoints and, used as an execution gate, reduced executed unsafe effects from 43.3% to 5.0% for one agent at a small cost to benign completion. We derive implications for designing consent around consequences rather than individual calls.
papers.title_ja: 許可されたアクションが禁止されたワークフローを完了させる場合：LLMエージェント向けに結果志向の承認設計を行う
papers.summary_ja: LLMエージェントにおける「累積的認可失敗」問題、すなわち個々のアクションは許可されているが、それらが組み合わさると禁止された結果を招く現象に対処する。論文では、ユーザーの意図を再提示し、アクションと結果を紐付け、累積的な影響を可視化する「Cumulative Consent Ledger (CCL)」という承認インターフェースを提案する。80名を対象とした実験では、従来の時系列ログと比較してCCLの方が不安全な承認が少なく、理解度が高く、判断が速いことが示された。また、信頼できるモニターによるアーティファクトの系譜追跡により、違反チェックポイントの検出率が89.2%に達し、実行される不安全な影響を大幅に低減できることをシステム評価で実証した。

papers.title: Digital Knockoffs
papers.summary: Social simulations often use language model agents to represent people who differ on several measurable traits. However, describing a trait profile in a prompt does not guarantee the agent will express each trait at its intended level. We propose a method that calibrates agents to multidimensional profiles using activation steering: (i) extract steering directions for each trait, (ii) learn a shared mapping from steering strengths to measured trait scores, and (iii) search for a steering intervention for each target. We use Bayesian optimization for this search and evaluate the method on the Big Five personality scores of 500 OpenPsychometrics respondents. In each of five rounds, the assigned interventions yield lower mean absolute error across respondents than the prompting and steering baselines. Further, the model's responses to a given intervention yield the same trait profile regardless of whose target motivated it, so a poor match for one respondent can be the best match for another. When we match each respondent to the closest profile found across all tested interventions, Bayesian optimization yields 16.6% lower mean absolute error than uniform random search at the same evaluation budget. Our method thus offers a way to build social agents whose measured traits dovetail with those of the people they seek to represent. Whether this closer fit translates to improved predictions of downstream behavior remains an open question.
papers.title_ja: デジタルの模倣品
papers.summary_ja: LLMエージェントの性格特性（ビッグファイブなど）を意図したレベルで正確に表現させるための新しいキャリブレーション手法を提案する。アクティベーション・スチアリングを用いて特性ベクトルを抽出し、ベイズ最適化により介入強度を探索することで、プロンプトや単純なスチアリングより高い精度で目標特性を再現する。500人の被験者データを用いた評価では、ランダム探索比で平均絶対誤差を16.6%低減し、エージェントの特性が実在人物とより密接に一致することを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMエージェント設計とベイズ最適化の組み合わせが関心に直結

papers.title: Don't Train It, Write It: An AI Agent Writes New Capabilities into Language Model Weights
papers.summary: We show that an AI agent can write new capabilities into a pretrained language model by adding gated attention heads and MLP neurons inside its existing layers, without backpropagation and without fitting any weight to the answers of task examples. It has a budget of 50 model passes and sees no validation or test instance. Composed in one model, its modules for six BIG-Bench Hard (BBH) subtasks raise the normalized BBH score of Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct from 19.95 to 41.05 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: at most 35.01) and that of Gemma-3-1B-it from 10.25 to 32.86. Against the unmodified model at the same precision, both composites leave the next-token distribution on 1,023,000 WikiText tokens unchanged (KL exactly 0), give identical answers on 15,845 items of five other Leaderboard tests and identical scores on the other 18 BBH subtasks. The agent also writes exact multiplication up to 20 digits, running the model only up to 6 (100.0% on the absent lengths of the sealed test in both models; a LoRA with the same budget: at most 2.1%). Sets, rules and report sentences were sealed in git before the first session (manifests timestamped in Bitcoin), with dated amendments listed in Appendix D; a frozen evaluator ran the sealed test once. Verdicts (H5: tracking; H6: composite; H8: one pass vs. chain of thought; H9: fresh and rewritten instances; H10: side effects; H12: multiplication), on the preregistered sealed test, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct: H5 success, H6 success, H8 (web_of_lies) success, H9 success, H10 (composite) success on (i) to (iii), (iv) confirmed, H12 success; Gemma-3-1B-it (H7: H5, H6, H8 and H9 in this model): H5 success, H6 success, H8 (web_of_lies) success, H8 (tracking 3) success, H9 partial, H10 (composite) success on (i) to (iii), (iv) confirmed, H12 success. Not everything worked: 4 of 45 single modules show small side effects and 5 of 50 sessions hit the 12-hour limit without a module.
papers.title_ja: 学習せず、記述する：AIエージェントが言語モデルの重みに新機能を埋め込む
papers.summary_ja: バックプロパゲーションや重み調整を行わず、既存の層内にゲート付きアテンションヘッドやMLPニューロンを追加することで、AIエージェントがLLMに新しい能力を付与する手法を提案する。Qwen2.5やGemma-3などのモデルにおいて、BIG-Bench Hardのスコアを大幅に向上させつつ、他のタスクでの性能劣化や分布変化をゼロに抑えることを実証した。さらに、20桁までの正確な乗算処理など、従来のLoRAでは達成困難な高度な計算能力も、わずか50回のモデルパス予算内で実現した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの効率化・推論高速化・エージェント設計の交差点に位置する革新的手法

papers.title: From Reward Engineering to Data-Centric Reinforcement Learning for Effective Agentic Visual Tool Use
papers.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) increasingly use external visual tools to acquire evidence during reasoning, yet learning when to invoke these tools remains challenging. Existing tool-use reinforcement learning (RL) methods often rely on call-contingent rewards to encourage beneficial tool use, but such reward engineering can distort the task objective and lead to degenerate calling behaviors. We argue that effective tool-use learning requires identifying not merely which questions are difficult, but which failures are attributable to missing visual evidence and can therefore be corrected through tool observations. We propose AOVO, a data-centric framework that enables MLLMs to learn effective tool use through perception attribution and policy-adaptive data sampling (PADS), without introducing tool-specific rewards. It counterfactually probes the model's reasoning states to identify observation-sensitive questions, distinguishing them from reasoning-dominated ones. PADS then periodically estimates category-level observation effects from recent policy rollouts and dynamically reallocates the training distribution toward questions where visual observations provide informative learning signals, while optimizing solely for final-answer correctness. Experiments across diverse visual perception and multimodal reasoning benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over competitive tool-use MLLMs, with causal analysis further validating the data-centric perspective for learning effective visual tool use.
papers.title_ja: 報酬設計からデータ中心の強化学習へ：効果的なエージェント型視覚ツール利用のためのアプローチ
papers.summary_ja: マルチモーダル大規模言語モデル（MLLM）における視覚ツールの利用学習において、従来の報酬設計がもたらす劣化行動を解消するデータ中心型フレームワーク「AOVO」を提案する。モデルの推論状態を反事実的にプローブし、視覚証拠の欠如が失敗の原因である「観察敏感型」質問を特定する。これにより、ツール固有の報酬を導入せず、最終回答の正しさのみを最適化しながら、学習分布を動的に再配分する。多様なベンチマークで既存手法を上回る性能を示し、因果分析によりデータ中心アプローチの有効性を検証した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMのエージェント設計と強化学習、ツール利用の最適化に直結する手法

papers.title: Tool-to-Self: Internalizing Visual Tool Capabilities via Scaffolded Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) increasingly rely on external visual tools to access fine-grained visual evidence, but repeated tool execution incurs substantial inference overhead and deployment dependencies. Moreover, conventional tool-use RL can improve visual-task performance, yet the resulting tool gains are often unstable. Motivated by this, we propose Tool-to-Self (T2S), a tool-scaffolded reinforcement learning framework that turns external visual tools into temporary training scaffolds. T2S cold-starts tool-use ability and observation prediction from tool-repairable examples, then progressively anneals tool execution on a per-tool basis during RL. By combining answer-correctness and observation-consistency rewards with privileged on-policy self-distillation from actual tool observations, T2S effectively teaches the model both to reproduce tool outputs and to reason from them. Experiments across diverse visual perception and reasoning benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over both explicit tool-use models and implicit zooming models while enabling tool-free inference with reduced latency.
papers.title_ja: ツールから自己へ：スキャフォールド型強化学習による視覚ツール機能の内部化
papers.summary_ja: 視覚言語モデル（VLM）が外部ツールに依存する際の推論オーバーヘッドと不安定性を解決するため、ツールを訓練用の足場として活用する強化学習フレームワーク「Tool-to-Self (T2S)」を提案する。ツール実行を段階的に減衰させながら、ツール出力の再現とそれに基づく推論を同時に学習させることで、モデル内部にツール機能を内包させる。多様な視覚認識・推論ベンチマークにおいて、明示的なツール使用モデルや暗黙的なズームモデルを上回る性能を示しつつ、ツール不要の高速推論を実現した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM推論高速化と強化学習手法の組み合わせが関心に直結

papers.title: Understanding and Mitigating the Fragility of Self-Rewarding Optimization
papers.summary: Self-rewarding optimization (SRO) promises to improve language models by enabling them to generate their own reward signals. Yet when and how SRO succeeds or fails remains poorly understood. We reveal that SRO is fundamentally fragile: even seemingly benign perturbations to training prompts can corrupt the self-generated preference signal and trigger iterative collapse. We demonstrate this through two prompt-level attacks that serve as controlled stress tests: a Re-Ranking attack that concentrates training on prompts where self-reward diverges from an oracle, and a Preamble attack that learns short prefixes inflating self-reward without any gain in oracle quality. To explain why these attacks succeed, we introduce self-reward fidelity (SRF), a metric quantifying on-policy agreement between self-evaluated and oracle rewards. We show that SRF can serve as a diagnostic signal of self-supervision reliability, and that controlled SRF perturbations induce a phase-transition region: SRO improves when SRF remains sufficiently high, but collapses once SRF drops below a model- and task-dependent threshold. This analysis motivates Projection Decoupling Defense, which suppresses SRO update components along directions to which the reward generator is locally sensitive, improving SRO robustness under adversarial conditions. This work sheds light on the fragility of SRO and charts promising directions toward making it more robust.
papers.title_ja: 自己報酬最適化の脆性の理解と緩和
papers.summary_ja: 自己報酬最適化（SRO）が学習プロンプトの微小な摂動に対して極めて脆弱であることを示し、自己生成された報酬シグナルの破綻と反復的崩壊のメカニズムを解明した。自己報酬とオラクル報酬の一致度を定量化する指標「自己報酬忠実度（SRF）」を提案し、これが信頼性の診断シグナルとして機能することを示した。SRFが閾値を下回るとSROが崩壊する相転移領域が存在することを明らかにし、報酬生成器が局所的に敏感な方向の更新成分を抑制する「射影分離防御」により、敵対的条件下でのSROの頑健性を向上させる手法を提示した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの自己改善手法の脆弱性分析と防御策であり、モデル効率化・安定化に直結する。

papers.title: Bridging Teacher-Student Capability Gaps with Recurrent Computation
papers.summary: Knowledge distillation transfers capabilities from large language models to smaller students, yet stronger teachers do not always yield better students. Recent studies report diminishing or even negative returns from teacher scaling. We hypothesize that these limitations arise in part from insufficient student capacity to absorb the teacher's knowledge. We therefore investigate loop and recurrent computation as a way to expand the student's effective capacity by modifying its computation graph while keeping the backbone parameter count fixed. Under teacher-forced KD during pretraining, weight-shared looping improves performance but retains teacher-size saturation, whereas cross-token recurrence avoids the observed reversal with larger teachers. In mathematical post-training under both teacher-forced KD and on-policy distillation (OPD), recurrent students scale better with increasing teacher size than looped and vanilla LLMs do. Crucially, we show that a pretrained LLM can be readily fine-tuned into a looped or recurrent architecture jointly with OPD, without repeating pretraining. Our recurrent Qwen model improves with larger teachers and consistently outperforms looped and vanilla LLMs. This suggests a new post-training paradigm that integrates architectural conversion into distillation, avoiding a separate conversion stage while substantially improving student performance and maintaining near-vanilla inference latency.
papers.title_ja: 再帰計算による教師-生徒間の能力ギャップの解消
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）の知識蒸留において、教師モデルの規模拡大が必ずしも生徒モデルの性能向上に繋がらない問題に対し、計算グラフを変更して有効な容量を拡張する手法を提案する。バックボーンのパラメータ数を固定したままループや再帰計算を導入し、特にトークン間再帰が教師モデルのスケールメリットを維持することを示した。事前学習済みLLMを再帰アーキテクチャへ変換し、オンポリシー蒸留と併せて微調整することで、追加の事前学習なしで性能を向上させる新しいポストトレーニングパラダイムを実現した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM効率化・蒸留・推論高速化の核心手法であり、ユーザー関心と高度に一致

papers.title: Rollout Scheduling for Chaotic Neural ODEs: Coverage Gains, Computational Cost, and Predictive Accuracy
papers.summary: Training Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Neural ODEs) on chaotic systems is difficult because small changes in model parameters can lead to rapidly growing differences in predictions. A rollout is a trajectory predicted by the model. Choosing its length from a single global Lyapunov time overlooks differences in local instability. We study rollout scheduling for training on one contiguous rollout per sampled state, asking whether adapting its length to local instability improves prediction. We find the schedule that uses the most trajectory data under an instability budget, a limit on how much instability any one rollout may accumulate. Under stated assumptions, we bound the resulting coverage gain and the coverage lost when the instability estimates are in error. Numerical checks illustrate the theory. Training experiments on Lorenz-63, Lorenz-96, and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky compare adaptive and constant schedules at the same instability budgets and maximum rollout lengths. The budgets are computed from the true system's finite-time Lyapunov exponents. Across the tested settings, adaptive schedules increase trajectory coverage at additional computational cost, without showing a consistent improvement in prediction accuracy. On Lorenz-63, limiting adaptive rollouts to the horizon used to estimate instability improves prediction at the larger budgets. On Kuramoto--Sivashinsky, most configurations provide useful short-time predictions, while all tested long rollouts eventually fail. These findings show why coverage, prediction accuracy, and long-time behavior need separate evaluation, and why instability estimates should be checked over the windows used in training.
papers.title_ja: カオティックなニューラルODEにおけるロールアウトスケジューリング：カバレッジ向上、計算コスト、予測精度
papers.summary_ja: カオス系におけるニューラルODEの学習において、局所的不安定性に応じてロールアウト長を適応させる手法を提案する。不安定性予算の制約下で、カバレッジ向上と予測精度のトレードオフを理論的に解析し、Lorenz系やKuramoto-Sivashinsky系で検証した。結果、適応スケジューリングはカバレッジを向上させるが、予測精度の改善は一貫せず、計算コスト増と引き換えに長期的予測は依然として困難であることが示された。
papers.relevance_reason: 物理情報ニューラルネットとカオス系の予測精度評価に直結

papers.title: Neural Fidelity Calibration for Informative Sim-to-Real Adaptation
papers.summary: Deep reinforcement learning (RL) can transfer agile robot skills from simulation to the real world, but closing the sim-to-real gap by domain randomization requires expert physics knowledge, and simulator calibration from real data typically targets a few hand-picked parameters. Even then, simulators miss real-world effects, and environments reconstructed from onboard perception inherit sensing errors that limit policy improvement. We propose Neural Fidelity Calibration (NFC), which uses conditional flow matching to calibrate simulator physical parameters and residual fidelity domains online during deployment. Residual fidelity captures sim-to-real dynamics discrepancies and perception-induced environment uncertainty. NFC operates in a latent space so that realistic environments can be sampled from the inferred posterior for real-to-sim policy fine-tuning. The framework is informative: the pretrained policy is fine-tuned only when an anomaly is detected, sequential NFC seeds its proposal from the simulation-pretrained estimator, and a hallucination policy modulates posterior uncertainty following optimism in the face of uncertainty. NFC attains the most accurate posteriors among established simulation-based inference methods on five robots with up to 39 physical parameters and a 128x128 residual terrain. On a wheeled robot with a broken wheel axle deployed on snow, mud, and wet grass, NFC raises success on rough terrain from 26% to 70% and reduces orientation jerk by 88%. Code and videos will be released upon publication.
papers.title_ja: 情報的シミュレーションから実環境への適応のためのニューラルフィデリティキャリブレーション
papers.summary_ja: 深層強化学習によるロボット制御において、シミュレーションと実環境のギャップを埋めるための新しい手法「NFC」を提案する。条件付きフローマッチングを用いて、物理パラメータと残差フィデリティ（環境不確実性）をオンラインでキャリブレーションし、潜在空間で現実的な環境をサンプリングする。異常検知時のみポリシーをファインチューニングし、ハルシネーション対策として不確実性に対する楽観主義を適用する。5種類のロボットで既存手法より高精度な事後分布を得て、雪や泥などの粗悪地での成功률을26%から70%へ向上させた。
papers.relevance_reason: 強化学習・シミュレーション・ハルシネーション対策の複合領域であり、ユーザーの関心に高度に一致する。

papers.title: Handover Cost Optimization in LEO Satellite Networks using an RL-based Multiple-Column Selection Strategy via Branch-and-Price
papers.summary: Next-generation wireless networks increasingly rely on low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites for broad coverage and low latency, making efficient handover management essential. We formulate satellite handover as a combinatorial optimization problem, assigning each ground user to exactly one capacity-limited, visible satellite while minimizing network handover costs. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL)-based branch-and-price (B&P) framework with learned multiple-column selection (MCS) to accelerate column generation while retaining exact dynamic programming pricing. We also develop two lightweight heuristic policies: handover-aware visibility duration (HAVD) for online decisions and congestion-aware predictive (CAP) for offline planning. Additionally, a local-search repair algorithm adapts precomputed B&P or MCS-B&P solutions to demand perturbations through single-flip and per-user trajectory re-optimization, avoiding complete re-optimization. Simulations using realistic large scale constellations, including Starlink Gen-1, demonstrate that MCS-B&P achieves solution quality comparable to exact B&P with fewer column-generation iterations, fewer branch-and-bound nodes, and reduced computation time. HAVD and CAP offer effective online and offline cost-latency trade-offs, while local-search repair recovers most performance losses due to demand perturbations at a fraction of the computational cost of full re-optimization.
papers.title_ja: 分枝価格法と強化学習ベースの複数カラム選択戦略を用いたLEO衛星ネットワークにおけるハンドオーバーコスト最適化
papers.summary_ja: LEO衛星ネットワークにおけるハンドオーバー管理を組合せ最適化問題として定式化し、強化学習（RL）を用いた分枝価格法（B&P）フレームワークを提案する。学習された複数カラム選択（MCS）によりカラム生成を高速化しつつ、厳密な動的計画法によるプライシングを維持する。さらに、オンライン・オフライン対応の軽量ヒューリスティックと、需要変動への適応を可能にする局所探索修復アルゴリズムも開発した。Starlink Gen-1などの大規模コンステレーションでのシミュレーションにより、計算時間を短縮しつつ厳密解に近い品質を達成することを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: RLと最適化手法の組み合わせだが、対象が衛星通信であり軌道力学ではないため

papers.title: LoKiTO: Local Kinodynamic Trajectory Optimization for UAVs based on Memory-Efficient Neural Distance Fields
papers.summary: This paper introduces LoKiTO, a 3D local kinodynamic trajectory optimizer that combines a Chebyshev polynomial parameterization with an online neural Euclidean Signed Distance Field (ESDF) representation for aerial robotics. While current gradient-based planners often struggle with the high memory requirements of explicit volumetric maps or fail to strictly enforce dynamic limits, LoKiTO embeds kinodynamic constraints directly into a modular cost function and exploits the numerical conditioning properties of the Chebyshev basis. Collision awareness is provided by a continuous, memory-efficient neural ESDF updated online from LiDAR measurements, which drastically reduces map memory consumption to approximately 1.0 MB. Benchmarking in highly cluttered simulated environments against state-of-the-art baselines (Fast-Planner and EGO-Planner) demonstrates the superiority of our approach. Experimental results show that LoKiTO achieves over 99.4% dynamic feasibility compliance, significantly outperforming the baselines, and maintaining higher median clearance from obstacles. By coupling a well-conditioned continuous parameterization with explicit kinodynamic reasoning, LoKiTO provides a practical and extensible basis for local replanning in aerial robotics.
papers.title_ja: LoKiTO: メモリ効率の良いニューラル距離場に基づくUAV向け局所運動学的軌道最適化
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、UAVの局所軌道最適化手法LoKiTOを提案する。チェビシェフ多項式によるパラメータ化と、LiDARデータからオンライン更新されるニューラルESDF（ユークリッド符号距離場）を組み合わせることで、メモリ消費を約1.0MBに抑えつつ、運動学的制約を厳密に満たす。混雑した環境でのベンチマークにより、既存手法より高い動的実現可能性と障害物クリアランスを達成したことを示す。
papers.relevance_reason: 軌道最適化とニューラル表現の組み合わせだが、航空機特化で宇宙分野とは異なる

papers.title: DriveTTO: Understanding Search and Selection in Test-Time Trajectory Optimization for End-to-End Driving
papers.summary: In difficult driving scenes, a learned scorer can select a poor trajectory from a fixed pool even when a better candidate is available. Nearby vehicles and road boundaries can also leave only a narrow range of high-scoring maneuvers. These constraints vary with the scene and are difficult to cover exhaustively during training. We introduce DriveTTO, a training-free method that searches around native proposals and checks each proposed refinement against a retained trajectory. A frozen scorer evaluates completed paths at the endpoints they actually reach, guiding resampling in progressively smaller neighborhoods. From a shared reference, one branch draws on planner proposals and another perturbs vehicle controls. DriveTTO blends their poses at matching times and accepts a branch or fusion update only when both frozen scorers predict a gain. On Navtest, DriveTTO recovers nonzero predictive driver model scores (PDMS) in 51.35% of native zero-score cases on average. Accounting for new failures, the zero-score rate falls from 1.63% to 1.13%. Benchmark-specific configurations achieve 95.54 PDMS and 92.30 extended PDMS (EPDMS) on Navtest, 57.10 EPDMS on Navhard, and 40.1 HD-Score on HUGSIM under observed commands. With a single frozen scorer, DriveTTO-S improves all six evaluated planners on both Navtest and Navhard.
papers.title_ja: DriveTTO: エンドツーエンド運転におけるテスト時軌道最適化の検索と選択の理解
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、学習済みスコアラーが固定候補から不適切な軌道を選択してしまう問題を解決するため、学習不要なテスト時最適化手法 DriveTTO を提案する。ネイティブ提案の周辺を段階的に狭い範囲で探索し、凍結されたスコアラーで評価しながら、プランナーの提案と車両制御の摂動を融合して軌道を改善する。Navtest などのベンチマークにおいて、ゼロスコアケースの回復率を向上させ、既存の 6 つのプランナーすべてで性能を改善したことを示している。
papers.relevance_reason: 軌道最適化と機械学習手法の組み合わせだが、対象が自動運転であり宇宙分野ではないため中程度。

papers.title: Real-Time Kinodynamic Multi-Agent Motion Planning
papers.summary: Coordinating large robot fleets, from warehouses to quadrotor swarms, requires collision-free trajectories that satisfy dynamic constraints and stay within speed and acceleration bounds. Existing kinodynamic multi-agent planners enforce these bounds during the search or through trajectory optimization after it, which limits fleet size and speed. We present Tickwise Actions to Kinodynamic Trajectories (TAKT), a framework that accounts for the dynamics before the search and reduces planning to a lattice search for double-integrator robots. TAKT analytically bounds the clearance lost when a discrete plan is smoothed and reserves this margin on the lattice. A closed-form convolution provably converts any valid plan into dynamically feasible trajectories with continuous-time collision avoidance. For robots spanning many lattice vertices, we introduce a diamond formulation that permits one-tick sideways yielding and adapt the Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) solvers PIBT and LaCAM to it. With 50 robots, our planners run over 2,000 times faster than the strongest baseline in 2D halls and over 100 times in 3D, with comparable or lower makespan and cost. They plan about a thousand robots in seconds in 2D, and tens of seconds in 3D, and replan up to a thousand robots in real time.
papers.title_ja: リアルタイム動力学制約付きマルチエージェント運動計画
papers.summary_ja: 大規模ロボット群の衝突回避と動力学制約（速度・加速度）を同時に満たすリアルタイム計画手法「TAKT」を提案する。探索前に動力学を考慮し、ラティス探索に帰着させることで、既存手法より大幅に高速化を実現した。解析的にクリアランスを境界付けし、閉形式の畳み込みにより連続時間での衝突回避を保証する。50台のロボットで2D環境では最速ベースライン比2000倍以上、3D環境では100倍以上高速であり、1000台規模のリアルタイム replanning も可能である。
papers.relevance_reason: 軌道力学とは異なるが、マルチエージェント最適化・高速化の手法として参考になる

papers.title: From Low-Dimensional Chaos to High-Dimensional Dynamics in Self-Attention Systems
papers.summary: Continuous-time particle models of self-attention are often studied under symmetry assumptions that yield a gradient structure and constrain the dynamics to convergence toward equilibria. We investigate the behavior of these systems beyond the gradient setting, considering autonomous projected self-attention models with constant query, key, and value matrices and particles constrained to an ellipse. For three particles, the equations define a vector field on the three-dimensional torus. We derive explicit synchronized periodic solutions and compute their Floquet multipliers, establishing the existence of non-gradient dynamics. Numerical explorations using bifurcation diagrams, Poincare sections, periodic-orbit continuation, a nd Lyapunov exponents reveal attracting periodic orbits, invariant-torus-like behavior, and strong evidence of chaos. We then construct higher-dimensional systems by coupling these low-dimensional building blocks through masked and multi-head attention mechanisms. We discuss the persistence of normally hyperbolic invariant manifolds under weak coupling and investigate how the coupling architecture influences the resulting dynamics. Numerical experiments reveal the emergence of additional expanding directions, including a 60-particle system in which 26 of the 40 computed Lyapunov exponents exceed 0.01. These results demonstrate the richness of the dynamical behavior possible in simplified self-attention systems and motivate further investigation of the invariant structures organizing their high-dimensional dynamics.
papers.title_ja: 自己注意システムにおける低次元カオスから高次元ダイナミクスへ
papers.summary_ja: 自己注意メカニズムの連続時間粒子モデルにおいて、勾配構造を仮定しない非線形ダイナミクスの振る舞いを解析した。3粒子系で同期周期解とフロケ乗数を導出し、カオス的な挙動の存在を数値的に確認した。さらに、マスク付きマルチヘッド注意機構を用いて低次元ブロックを結合し、高次元系における不変多様体の持続性と、60粒子系での強いカオス性（正のリアプノフ指数の多発）を明らかにした。

papers.title: PushMimic: Learning Adaptive Humanoid Box Pushing via Dynamic Motion Augmentation and Reference Distillation
papers.summary: Humanoid box pushing is challenging when the physical properties of the task, such as the box mass and the ramp inclination, are unknown before the push begins. This paper presents PushMimic, a framework that learns adaptive humanoid box pushing from a single level-ground kinematic reference motion. The learned policy adapts its pushing posture to these properties without observing them. PushMimic augments the reference motion into a dynamically feasible motion dataset over these properties with sampling-based trajectory optimization, and distills the dataset into one motion tracking policy in one stage of training. Simulation results over box masses from 5 to 15 kg and ramp inclinations up to 15 degrees show that PushMimic raises the success rate from 57.8% to 88.8% compared with a baseline that tracks the original reference motion. It also reduces the cost of push of the arms by 22%. Hardware experiments on a Unitree G1 humanoid show that the policy adapts its torso pitch during continuous pushing on an inclined treadmill, with box masses up to 19 kg and ramp inclinations up to 12.6 degrees. PushMimic therefore needs only one reference motion, instead of one for every box mass and ramp inclination.
papers.title_ja: PushMimic: 動的モーション拡張と参照蒸留による適応型ヒューマノイド箱押し学習
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、箱の質量や傾斜が未知の条件下でヒューマノイドが箱を押し運ぶための適応型ポリシー学習フレームワーク「PushMimic」を提案する。単一の運動参照モーションから、サンプリングベースの軌道最適化により動的に実現可能なモーションデータセットを生成し、これを1段階の学習で運動追従ポリシーに蒸留する手法を採用している。シミュレーションでは、ベースラインと比較して成功率を57.8%から88.8%へ向上させ、腕の運動コストを22%削減した。さらに、Unitree G1を用いた実機実験でも、最大19kgの箱と12.6度の傾斜に対して躯幹ピッチを適応させ、連続的な押し込み動作を成功させた。

papers.title: PhyMind: Physics-Informed Masked Autoencoding for EEG Foundation Models
papers.summary: EEG foundation models are pre-trained almost exclusively with masked reconstruction through a free-form decoder, sometimes with hand-crafted spectral targets added, as in MANAS-2. We study what happens when that decoder is replaced by a generative forward model of EEG. PhyMind keeps a standard masked transformer encoder, but its decoder must explain the masked signal through 68 cortical regions, each driven by damped stochastic oscillators and an aperiodic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, projected to the recording's own montage by a fixed boundary-element lead field evaluated per derivation. Training combines masked reconstruction with a Whittle spectral likelihood, an oscillator-dynamics residual, a minimum-norm source prior and a penalised neural residual. In a controlled comparison (same encoder, data, steps and seed), the physics decoder produces encoder tokens whose spectral content is far more linearly decodable than with a masked-autoencoder decoder or with the MANAS-2 objective: mean R^2 on a token-level spectral probe with amplitude-normalised targets is 0.67/0.77/0.77 on three datasets, against 0.24/0.50/0.50 (MAE) and 0.48/0.67/0.66 (MANAS-2 objective), approaching the released 92.8M-parameter MANAS-2 (0.71/0.81/0.80). Downstream gains in the controlled setting are small (four-task mean balanced accuracy 56.6 vs. 53.8 for MAE frozen, 63.8 vs. 62.7 fine-tuned). Region-level features from the physics decoder raise frozen four-class motor-imagery accuracy by 7-14 points, so a 7.2M-parameter model pre-trained on 3k hours of open EEG is comparable to the released MANAS-2 with frozen features (63.0 vs. 61.6). After full fine-tuning, MANAS-2 remains better (66.8 vs. 65.4 for our best model). The inferred sources do not reproduce the lateralisation that a classical inverse solution finds in motor imagery, so we do not claim anatomical interpretability. Code and weights are released.
papers.title_ja: PhyMind: EEG基盤モデルのための物理情報マスクオートエンコーディング
papers.summary_ja: EEG基盤モデルのデコーダを、減衰確率振動子とOrnstein-Uhlenbeck過程に基づく物理的前方モデルに置き換える手法を提案する。標準的なマスクトランスフォーマーエンコーダを維持しつつ、物理的制約付きデコーダにより、トークンのスペクトル内容の線形解読可能性を大幅に向上させた。制御された比較実験において、物理デコーダはMAEやMANAS-2の目的関数よりも優れたスペクトル探査性能を示し、凍結特徴量下では小規模モデルながらMANAS-2と同等以上の精度を達成した。ただし、完全ファインチューニング後の最終精度ではMANAS-2が依然として優位であり、解剖学的解釈可能性については古典的逆問題解と一致しないため主張していない。
papers.relevance_reason: 物理情報ニューラルネットの手法自体は関心領域だが、対象がEEGであり軌道力学やLLM効率化とは直接無関係。

papers.title: HKD-ACPA: Heterogeneous Knowledge Distillation Adversarial Cyber-Physical Attacks in Power Grids
papers.summary: Learning-based algorithms assist power-grid control centers in localizing transmission-line attacks, yet existing adversarial attacks typically require white-box access or repeated online queries. We study a practical zero-query setting in which an adversary coordinates physical, denial-of-service (DoS), and false data injection (FDI) attacks using only local measurements and historical detector outputs. To bridge the input-view asymmetry between local adversarial observations and DoS-masked control-center measurements, we propose Heterogeneous Knowledge Distillation Adversarial Cyber-Physical Attacks (HKD-ACPA). HKD-ACPA distills historical detector predictions into a heterogeneous graph surrogate ensemble and trains a residual calibration module to correct the view-induced logit discrepancy. Over this calibrated surrogate, we formulate sparse, magnitude-bounded FDI synthesis with a group-balanced objective that jointly induces missed detections and false alarms, and solve the resulting hybrid discrete--continuous problem via bi-level projected gradient-based proximal policy optimization (PGPPO). Experiments on the IEEE 30-bus and 118-bus systems show that HKD-ACPA outperforms all surrogate-based baselines across every sparsity budget and surpasses online-query attacks in eight of ten system--budget settings without querying the detector model.
papers.title_ja: HKD-ACPA: 電力網における異種知識蒸留を用いた敵対的サイバーフィジカル攻撃
papers.summary_ja: 電力網の制御センターにおける攻撃検出器に対する、ゼロクエリ環境での敵対的攻撃手法を提案する。局所観測と制御センターの観測間の非対称性を解消するため、過去の検出器出力から異種グラフサロゲートアンサンブルを構築し、残差補正モジュールでロジットのズレを調整する。この補正済みサロゲート上で、誤検知と検知漏れを同時に誘発するスパースな偽データ注入（FDI）を、二層計画問題として定式化する。IEEE 30バスおよび118バスシステムでの実験により、既存のサロゲートベース手法を上回る性能と、オンラインクエリ不要の効率的な攻撃能力を実証した。

papers.title: Attacking Tabular Foundation Models: An Experimental Taxonomy of Context Poisoning and Test-Time Evasion
papers.summary: Tabular foundation models condition predictions on labeled examples supplied at inference time, creating an attack surface that differs from conventional model training. We study four manipulation families (label flipping, backdoor context poisoning, clean-label context selection, and test-time evasion) and organize them by attack stage, label consistency, and distributional realism. TabPFN-2.5, TabICL, and XGBoost are evaluated on CIC-IDS2017 and N-BaIoT using a common preprocessing and evaluation pipeline. Backdoor context poisoning provides strong targeted control over the in-context models with little change in clean accuracy, whereas selecting real, correctly labeled boundary-crowding rows causes no systematic accuracy degradation up to a 20% bias fraction. A simplified surrogate-transfer constrained PGD attack inspired by, but not equivalent to, CAPGD also produces test-time evasion, outperforming equal-budget random noise in most settings. The comparison shows that attack effectiveness depends strongly on both where manipulation occurs and how much freedom the attacker has to alter the data.
papers.title_ja: 表形式ファウンデーションモデルへの攻撃：コンテキストポイズニングとテスト時回避の実験的分類
papers.summary_ja: 推論時にラベル付き例を条件とする表形式ファウンデーションモデル（TabPFN-2.5, TabICL等）に対する4つの攻撃手法を体系的に分析した。バックドアコンテキストポイズニングはクリーン精度を維持しつつ高い制御性を示すが、境界近傍の行選択による攻撃は20%のバイアス割合まで精度劣化を引き起こさないことが判明した。また、簡略化されたサロゲート転送制約付きPGD攻撃は、ランダムノイズを上回るテスト時回避能力を持つことを示した。攻撃の効率は、操作が行われる段階と攻撃者のデータ変更の自由度に強く依存する。

papers.title: Learning Land-Surface Hydrology World Model from Satellite Observations
papers.summary: A world model should tell us not only what will happen, but what would happen under a different action. Learned Earth models now forecast remarkably well, yet forecast skill says little about what their state means or how it responds to a changed driver. We build LandWM, a world model of land-surface water in which rain is the action, learned from seven years of SMAP and CYGNSS observations: physical observation operators tie its latent state to soil water, and a mass-conserving balance governs how that state responds to rain. Over the U.S. Southern Great Plains, the model, never shown a soil-moisture value, tracks 28 in-situ probes as well as the operational SMAP Level-4 product, even from CYGNSS alone, and a storm added to the forcing of a station's cell wets its soil as natural storms wet the probes. Replace either piece and the forecasts stay, but the meaning goes: with neural operators, only a probe fitted to the stations finds the soil water; with a generic recurrent transition, rain on a single cell barely moves it. Yet when the same rain covers the whole region the two transitions swap roles, and the conserving one responds too weakly. Grounding makes a world model readable; its response to actions must be tested under more than one kind of intervention.
papers.title_ja: 衛星観測から学習する陸地表層水文学の世界モデル
papers.summary_ja: 衛星観測データから学習した陸地表層の水循環に関する世界モデル「LandWM」を提案する。物理的な観測演算子と質量保存則に基づき、潜在状態を土壌水分と結びつけ、降雨という介入に対する応答性を確保した。米国南部大平原において、土壌水分の直接観測値を用いずに実測値と同等の精度で追跡し、局所的な降雨介入に対する物理的に妥当な反応を示した。ニューラルオペレータや汎用的な再帰遷移と比較し、物理的根拠（グラウンディング）がモデルの解釈可能性と介入への応答性に重要であることを示した。

papers.title: Distributionally-Verifiable Rewards for Human-Behavior Simulation
papers.summary: Large language models are increasingly used to simulate survey respondents in social-science research. A useful simulator should predict individual responses, reproduce population response distributions, and capture demographic differences. Common training approaches struggle to balance these goals: exact-match rewards encourage the model to concentrate on the most frequent human response, which is contradictory to the goal of distributional alignment. Meanwhile, aggregate distribution matching can look good even when demographic information is ignored. To this end, we introduce Distributionally-Verifiable Rewards (DVR), a reinforcement-learning reward that uses demographic group distribution gaps to guide individual responses, designed by aligning policy generated frequencies with human response frequencies within each question-group margins. We evaluate the method using the OpinionQA dataset and find that comparing with accuracy-only RLVR, DVR preserves per-response accuracy while reducing JSD by 34.5% in-distribution and 14.6% on held-out questions, with higher DPC point estimates on both splits. Comparing KL-SFT with the demographics-blind marginal further shows that low JSD is insufficient to establish fidelity to population heterogeneity, highlighting that accuracy, distributional fit, and demographic structure should be evaluated together.
papers.title_ja: 人間行動シミュレーションのための分布検証可能報酬
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）を用いた社会科学研究における回答者シミュレーションの精度向上を目的とした研究である。個々の回答の正確さと集団の分布特性、および人口統計学的な差異を同時に満たすための強化学習報酬手法「Distributionally-Verifiable Rewards (DVR)」を提案した。DVRは、人口統計グループごとの分布ギャップを指標として個々の回答を導くことで、単純な一致報酬や集計分布マッチングの限界を克服する。OpinionQAデータセットでの評価により、DVRは回答精度を維持しつつ、分布適合度（JSD）を大幅に改善し、人口統計構造への忠実性を高めることが示された。

papers.title: Feedback-Driven Prompt Refinement for Educational AI: Affective Trajectory Estimation and Bloom's Taxonomy Classification
papers.summary: Contribution: This study has shown that a shared prompt-refinement procedure, guided by distinct affective and cognitive feedback signals, can improve held-out reference agreement and multi-label classification while reducing affective-generation variability without executor parameter updates. Background: Industry 4.0 has increased demand for personalized technical education across interconnected computing and engineering domains, while prompt sensitivity and generation variability have complicated dependable interpretation of instructional dialogue and learning outcomes. Research Questions: The study has examined whether task-specific feedback can improve affective-reference agreement, generation consistency, and cognitive classification without updating executor parameters. Methodology: A secondary language model has revised executor prompts using executor-output discrepancies against model-generated affective references for four dialogues and annotated Bloom labels for 70 learning outcomes; separate sets of 100 EduTalk conversations and 1,000 outcomes have supported held-out comparisons. Small refinement sets, unvalidated affective references, and absent learner-outcome measures have constrained interpretation. Findings: Affective mean absolute error has decreased from 0.742 to 0.702 and mean generation standard deviation from 0.307 to 0.238, while Bloom micro-F1 has increased from 0.687 to 0.893 and exact-match subset accuracy from 0.418 to 0.636. These findings have supported prompt refinement as a candidate approach for developing adaptive technical instruction, while its effects on workforce learning remain to be established.
papers.title_ja: 教育AIにおけるフィードバック駆動のプロンプト改善：感情軌道の推定とブルームの分類法による分類
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、教育用AIにおけるプロンプトの感度と生成のばらつきを低減するため、感情と認知のフィードバック信号に基づいたプロンプト改善手法を提案する。パラメータ更新なしで、二次LLMを用いて実行LLMのプロンプトを修正し、感情の一致度とブルーム分類法の多ラベル分類精度を向上させた。結果として、感情の平均絶対誤差は0.742から0.702へ、生成の標準偏差は0.307から0.238へ減少し、ブルーム分類のマイクロF1は0.687から0.893へ向上した。この手法は、適応型技術教育の信頼性を高める有望なアプローチであるが、学習者への実際の影響は未検証である。

papers.title: ESM-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Whether AI Agents Understand Earth System Model Physics and Code
papers.summary: AI coding agents that modify Earth System Model (ESM) code must preserve both software interfaces and the physical assumptions encoded in them. We introduce ESM-Bench, a benchmark of 60 developer-commit tasks from 6 repositories: Noah-MP, CLM5, SUMMA, ParFlow, MOM6, and VIC. The v5 corpus contains 17 physics-based bug fixes, 16 process-representation modifications, 13 parameterization-scheme selections, and 14 parameter-optimization tasks. Each task includes a scientific objective, parent-commit source files, a reference diff, and three stored prompt variants. An artifact audit confirms that all 60 reference diffs apply to their supplied starting files. We define an eight-item patch-review rubric and audit five archived patch fixtures against the implemented local checkers. None of the five fixture diffs applies to its supplied starting files, yet three text-pattern checkers return a pass. A ParFlow expression replay disagrees with the reference slopes, and a MOM6 pattern check detects an omitted update. Inspection also identifies a retained VIC reference assignment that overwrites the intended vegetation-specific albedo. These findings expose limits of reference patches and local proxies as correctness evidence. The release provides a reproducible corpus and diagnostic tools; complete expert validation, comparative agent performance, and full-model execution remain unmeasured on v5.
papers.title_ja: ESM-Bench: 地球システムモデルの物理法則とコード理解を評価するためのAIエージェント向けベンチマーク
papers.summary_ja: 地球システムモデル（ESM）のコード修正において、ソフトウェアインターフェースと物理的仮定を両立させるAIコーディングエージェントの評価基準「ESM-Bench」を提案する。6つのリポジトリから抽出した60件の開発者コミットタスク（物理ベースのバグ修正、パラメータ最適化など）で構成される。パッチレビューのルーブリックと診断ツールを提供し、既存のローカルチェッカーや参照パッチが正解性を保証できない限界を特定した。完全な専門家検証やエージェント間の比較性能測定は未実施だが、再現可能なコーパスと診断ツールを公開している。

papers.title: Integrating a one-dimensional convolutional neural network with nonlinear model predictive control for slug flow modeling and control
papers.summary: Severe slugging in pipeline--riser systems degrades production efficiency and threatens equipment integrity, motivating the development of accurate yet deployable control models. This paper presents a lightweight, data-driven modeling and control framework specifically designed for slug flow. First, we revisit a commonly used low-order mechanistic model and introduce two changes that improve physical plausibility and numerical robustness: (i) an explicit zero-outflow boundary during the starvation period at the riser top, and (ii) a reformulated expression for the liquid volume fraction at the riser top that enforces admissible bounds. Synthetic input--output trajectories generated by this model are then used to train a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D CNN) that parameterizes a neural ODE with an affine-in-control. Training employs an 8-step free-roll objective on standardized data; a differential sensitivity check confirms an explicit control channel. The learned model is embedded in a shooting-based nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) scheme with bounded and rate-smoothed actuation. In closed-loop simulations at {\Delta}t = 0.1 second, the controller drives the output to a constant setpoint within approximately 15--18 seconds while maintaining smooth, bounded inputs and non-oscillatory transients. The results indicate that a simple 1D CNN, coupled with NMPC, can capture the characteristic oscillations and regime transitions of slug flow and deliver effective regulation with modest computational cost. Although training is conducted offline to ensure reproducibility, the architecture and identification procedure are designed for extension to online learning, providing a practical path toward adaptive slug-flow mitigation.
papers.title_ja: スラッグフローのモデリングと制御における1次元CNNと非線形モデル予測制御の統合
papers.summary_ja: パイプライン・ライザー系における深刻なスラッグフローを抑制するため、軽量なデータ駆動型モデリングと制御フレームワークを提案する。低次メカニスティックモデルから生成した合成データを用いて、制御に対してアフィンなニューラルODEをパラメータ化する1次元CNNを訓練した。学習済みモデルを射撃法ベースの非線形モデル予測制御（NMPC）に組み込むことで、閉ループシミュレーションにおいて約15〜18秒で定常値に収束し、滑らかで有界な制御入力を維持した。計算コストを抑えつつスラッグフローの振動とレジーム遷移を捉える有効性を示し、オンライン学習への拡張可能性も示唆している。

papers.title: The Value of Labels in Data Selection for Least Squares
papers.summary: Suppose a selector sees a finite labelled dataset and chooses $n$ of its rows, with repetition. Ordinary least squares is then fitted to the rows that were chosen, without weights, and the excess loss of the fit on the full dataset is measured in units of the optimal loss. Without further assumptions this ratio does not decay with $n$. We examine the problem for $d$ features and rows of normalized leverage at most $\kappa$, and determine or bound the leading constants. A selector that must establish its rule before seeing the labels has an optimal worst-case ratio of $d\kappa/n$ to leading order, whatever use it makes of the features. With scalar labels, a selector that sees the labels achieves a value between $d\kappa/(2n)$ and $d\kappa\Lambda_d/n$, where $\Lambda_d<1$ is the rounding constant of mean selection. For $d\le4$, the constant is then $d\kappa/2$, so that labels are worth exactly a factor of two there, and for one feature and $m$ outputs it is $\kappa\Lambda_m$. With two or more features the selector can change the proportions of the frequent rows and therefore reshape its own design matrix. We design a simplified optimization problem, which we call a game, that bounds the constant for datasets with exactly fitted frequent rows, then show that its value is at most one half of the gradient energy in several regimes, and that one half is exact along directions in which the frequent rows are rigid, such as an intercept. For grouped designs, in which reshaping amounts to the allocation of a common budget, the constant is $27d/128$ up to an additive constant, compared with $d$ without labels. Nevertheless, one half is not the constant in every dimension: we construct datasets of extremely high dimension and large leverage on which every selection has an excess ratio of at least $(e^{-1/2}-o(1))\,d\kappa/n$, so that labels are worth at most a factor close to $\sqrt e$ there.
papers.title_ja: 最小二乗法におけるデータ選択時のラベルの価値
papers.summary_ja: 有限のラベル付きデータセットから行を選択し、最小二乗法を適用した場合の過剰損失（excess loss）の理論的上界を解析する。ラベルを見ずに選択する場合と、ラベルを見て選択する場合の最適比を比較し、特徴量次元 $d$ と最大レバレッジ $κ$ を用いた定数項を特定した。ラベルの利用により、低次元では損失が最大で2倍改善されることを示し、高次元や特定の設計では改善率が $√ e$ 倍程度に制限されることを証明した。
papers.relevance_reason: 機械学習の基礎理論だが、LLMや軌道力学への直接適用は薄い

papers.title: torchtsetlin: Fast, Interpretable Tsetlin Machines for PyTorch
papers.summary: The Tsetlin machine learns propositional rules with teams of Tsetlin automata that are driven by reward and penalty rather than gradients, so its models are interpretable by construction and cheap to evaluate. Its software, however, consists of C and CUDA kernels behind scikit-learn-style wrappers that sit outside the deep learning ecosystem. torchtsetlin implements the Tsetlin machine family as ordinary PyTorch modules: vanilla and weighted, coalesced, regression, convolutional over sequences, images and volumes, and dense per-pixel segmentation. The automata are a tensor buffer, so a model moves with .to(device), is saved with state_dict() and learns from a mini-batch with one update(x,y) call. Its core technique is a batched formulation of Type I and Type II feedback, in which automaton transitions become event counts realised as binomial draws, with one commit per mini-batch. On ten benchmarks taken from the existing libraries, it matches their accuracy, and on all but the two smallest it trains 2.4-10.9X faster than PyTsetlinMachineCUDA and 10.3-81.2X faster than tmu on the same GPU. The package is pure Python, MIT-licensed and on PyPI; every number in this paper is reproduced by one script. Code: https://github.com/vlbthambawita/torchtsetlin; package: https://pypi.org/project/torchtsetlin/.
papers.title_ja: torchtsetlin: PyTorch による高速かつ解釈可能な Tsetlin マシンの実装
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、報酬とペナルティ駆動で解釈可能性を備える Tsetlin マシンを PyTorch モジュールとして実装したパッケージ「torchtsetlin」を提案する。従来の C/CUDA 依存を排除し、テンソルバッファとして自動遷移を管理することで、標準的な PyTorch ワークフロー（デバイス移動、state_dict 保存、ミニバッチ学習）にシームレスに統合可能にした。Type I/II フィードバックのバッチ化により、既存ライブラリと同等の精度を維持しつつ、GPU 上で最大 81 倍の学習高速化を実現した。純粋な Python 実装であり、再現性のあるベンチマーク結果を提供している。

papers.title: Learning the Projection onto the Data Support: Distribution Learning that Avoids Memorization
papers.summary: We introduce a framework for learning distributions supported on manifolds based on estimating the nearest-point projection onto the data support. Specifically, we define an objective functional over a class of functions whose minimizer recovers this projection. The proposed framework automatically adapts to the intrinsic dimension and allows for data supported on unions of manifolds with varying dimensions. The resulting objective can be optimized using standard neural network architectures. We present population-level results establishing recovery of the manifold projection and prove finite-sample Wasserstein generalization bounds. Furthermore, we validate the approach empirically across a range of settings. In contrast to widely used generative models such as diffusion models, whose objectives can be minimized by memorizing training samples, our formulation excludes such behavior. We also introduce a direct memorization metric to verify that the learned projection generates new samples rather than reproducing the training set.
papers.title_ja: データサポートへの射影の学習：暗記を回避する分布学習
papers.summary_ja: マンifold上にサポートを持つ分布を、データサポートへの最近点射影を推定することで学習するフレームワークを提案する。この手法は固有次元に自動適応し、標準的なニューラルネットワークで最適化可能である。拡散モデルなど一般的な生成モデルが持つ訓練データ暗記の問題を構造的に排除し、新しいサンプル生成能力を直接検証する指標も導入している。

papers.title: Variable Importance Recovery in Tabular Foundation Models: A Simulation Study
papers.summary: In machine learning, identifying which variables contribute predictive information can be as important as predictive accuracy. Tabular foundation models have matched or exceeded the predictive performance of tuned gradient boosting trees on many small- and medium-sized tabular datasets. Yet their ability to recover population-level variable importance has received little attention. We design and conduct a Monte Carlo simulation study to compare variable importance recovery across tabular foundation models and established machine learning baselines. Our framework distinguishes multiple population estimands, pairs each one with an aligned model-agnostic importance estimator, and evaluates recovery in terms of ranking, support, and relative magnitude. Our results show that tabular foundation models are generally competitive with established machine-learning baselines in recovering population variable importance, and often more accurate. We thus extend the evidence for their capabilities to a previously underexamined dimension, further strengthening their appeal.
papers.title_ja: 表形式ファウンデーションモデルにおける変数重要度の復元：シミュレーション研究
papers.summary_ja: 表形式データ向けのファウンデーションモデルが、予測精度だけでなく集団レベルの変数重要度をどの程度正確に復元できるかをモンテカルロシミュレーションで評価した。既存の機械学習ベースラインと比較し、ランキング・サポート・相対的な大きさの観点から重要度の復元能力を分析した。結果として、ファウンデーションモデルは既存手法と同等以上の性能を示し、多くの場合でより正確な重要度復元が可能であることが示された。これにより、表形式ファウンデーションモデルの適用範囲が予測性能から解釈可能性・変数選択まで拡大されることを裏付けている。

papers.title: What Do Differentiable Rule Learners Need? FLARE: Fuzzy Rules with Additive Evidence
papers.summary: Rule learners are used where transparency and accountability are required, because they give practitioners patterns they can read. Learning rules is a discrete problem, so neurosymbolic pipelines that use rules as explanations rely on relaxations such as the straight-through estimator. However, these differentiable rule learners often lag behind both classical rule learners and black-box classifiers in terms of performance. We study which parts of a rule-based classifier affect performance, and how well gradient-based training learns each of them. We found that most of the performance comes from how the rules are weighted: random rules with learned weights are already more accurate than every published differentiable rule learner we tested. Based on our results, we propose FLARE (Fuzzy Learned-Antecedent Rule Evidence), a differentiable rule learner that learns simple rules that combine to make the final decision. We also propose a learned encoding for variables with thousands of categories. We test FLARE on tabular data, using 42 datasets of OpenML-CC18 and the 38 classification tasks of TabArena. On CC18, FLARE exceeds the compared rule learners by 7.69 to 12.38 macro-F1 points and performs comparably to random forests, while remaining 1.00 to 1.11 points below tuned gradient-boosted trees. On TabArena it ranks at the same level as random forests and ahead of the other rule learners. As the concept-to-label head of a concept bottleneck model, FLARE is the best rule-based head in five of six settings. On graphs, it is competitive on PubMed and EMOGI but falls behind graph neural networks on Cora and Citeseer. Our code is available at https://github.com/Fuminides/FLARE
papers.title_ja: 微分可能なルール学習者に何が必要か？FLARE：加法証拠を用いたファジールール
papers.summary_ja: 本研究は、透明性と説明責任が求められる場面で利用される微分可能なルール学習者の性能劣化要因を分析し、ルールの重み付けが性能に最も大きく寄与することを明らかにした。この知見に基づき、単純なルールを組み合わせることで最終判断を行う微分可能なルール学習手法FLARE（Fuzzy Learned-Antecedent Rule Evidence）を提案する。さらに、数千のカテゴリを持つ変数に対する学習済みエンコーディングも導入した。OpenML-CC18やTabArenaなどの表形式データセットでの評価により、FLAREは既存のルール学習者よりも大幅に高精度であり、ランダムフォレストと同等の性能を示す一方、チューニング済みの勾配ブースティングツリーにはわずかに劣る結果となった。

papers.title: Temporal Logic Tensor Networks: Foundations of Temporal Reasoning in Neural Networks
papers.summary: In dynamic scenes---football matches, traffic streams, surgery, or assembly---actions unfold at fundamentally different time scales: in football, a kick happens in milliseconds, a possession lasts seconds, and complex events such as a successful pass followed by a goal combine multiple atomic actions over extended durations. Models trained solely on visual data struggle to learn effectively across different time scales, lacking a principled way of reasoning across fine-grained instants and broader intervals. Neither point-wise nor purely interval semantics suffices: the former fragments events into frame-level snapshots lacking overall event identification; the latter treats intervals as atomic truth-values, ignoring state trajectories. We introduce Temporal Logic Tensor Networks (tLTN), a differentiable neuro-symbolic framework addressing this duality via a formal, multi-sorted logic where events and states are structurally interdependent. Extending Interval Logic Tensor Networks (ILTN), tLTN grounds state predicates as fuzzy truth-value paths over time points, while events are first-class entities with learnable trapezoidal fuzzy durations and differentiable Allen-style relations. A compositional semantics fuses static, event-structural, and state-dynamic satisfaction into a single differentiable LTN grounding. Crucially, the modalities constrain each other bidirectionally: the interval layer dictates where point-wise constraints (e.g., Until, Since) are evaluated, restricting them to event-defined spans; conversely, the point-wise layer validates interval relations, rejecting them if underlying state dynamics contradict the relation. Through controlled synthetic examples, we show when single-modality learning fails and how this localization reduces frame-level computational cost on long traces.
papers.title_ja: 時間論理テンソルネットワーク：ニューラルネットワークにおける時間推論の基礎
papers.summary_ja: 動的シーンにおける異なる時間スケールのアクションを統合的に扱うため、微分可能なニューロシンボリックフレームワーク「tLTN」を提案する。イベントと状態を構造的に相互依存させる多様論理を用い、イベントの持続時間を学習可能な台形型ファジィ値として表現する。区間層と点層が双方向に制約し合うことで、長期間のトレースにおけるフレームレベルの計算コストを低減しつつ、時間的な一貫性を保つ推論を実現する。

papers.title: Scheduling of Variable-Speed Pumped Storage via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Variable-speed pumped storage hydropower (VSPSH) plants modulate power continuously in both generation and pumping, a match for the net-load ramps of rising wind and solar. Their flexibility is bounded by hydraulics rather than by a power rating, so the deliverable power range shifts with net head and excludes small outputs entirely. This paper addresses bidding and dispatch for such a plant across a two-settlement market with a hierarchical reinforcement-learning formulation. Its two layers are circularly dependent: a real-time (RT) bid is defined only against a cleared day-ahead (DA) commitment, and the DA reward only against an RT dispatch policy. Our proposed feasibility-constrained domain randomization breaks the cycle by training the RT layer on generated deliverable DA schedules before any bidding policy exists; the DA layer then optimizes against that frozen RT behavior, and the two alternate. Learning a policy at once profitable and deliverable is obstructed by the nonconvex operating region: penalizing infeasibility competes against the revenue the offer earns, discouraging an undeliverable offer without preventing one. We therefore pursue safety through action-space modification rather than through the reward, combining action masking of the bid space, projection of each commitment before settlement, and replacement by a fail-safe controller. Over 48 out-of-sample days it earns $3,313/day more than an equivalent penalty formulation while holding undeliverable commitment at a median of zero, which the penalty formulation does not, and no ablation improves on it without giving up deliverability or the storage target.
papers.title_ja: 階層型強化学習による可変速度揚水発電のスケジューリング
papers.summary_ja: 可変速度揚水発電所の日前市場とリアルタイム市場における入札・運用を、階層型強化学習で最適化する手法を提案する。非凸な運転領域による実行可能性の制約に対し、報酬関数へのペナルティではなく、アクション空間のマスクや射影、フェイルセーフ制御による安全性確保を行う。48日間のアウトオブサンプル評価において、従来のペナルティ手法より1日あたり3,313ドルの収益向上を実現し、実行不能な入札を中央値ゼロに抑えた。

papers.title: ArrythML-II: An Optimized TinyML Framework for ECG Arrhythmia Detection and Multi-Class Beat Classification on Wearable Devices
papers.summary: This paper presents ArrythML-II, an optimized TinyML framework for on-device ECG arrhythmia detection and multi-class beat classification on wearable platforms. A systematic hyperparameter optimization framework is developed to identify compact autoencoder architectures for binary ECG arrhythmia detection. A custom scoring mechanism jointly considers detection performance, reconstruction-error thresholds, and model size to guide architecture selection. The framework is further extended to six-class ECG beat classification using a lightweight classifier derived from the optimized autoencoder architecture. Both models are INT8 quantized and deployed using TensorFlow Lite Micro on a custom-developed, battery-operated, single-lead ECG device based on the PSoC~6 microcontroller. The deployed autoencoder and classifier have model sizes of approximately 44~KB and 22~KB, respectively, with end-to-end processing times of 5.1~ms and 4.7~ms per ECG segment. Model inference accounts for 3.95~ms and 1.38~ms of these processing times, respectively. In the refined arrhythmia detection evaluation using the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, the autoencoder achieved an accuracy of 84.76\%, precision of 82.68\%, and recall of 77.99\%. The multi-class classifier achieved 82.29\% accuracy, weighted precision of 90.18\%, and weighted recall of 82.29\%. Beyond offline model evaluation, the wearable platform is validated using preloaded ECG segments, live ECG signals, and an ESP32-S3-based ECG emulator that replays annotated MIT-BIH recordings as analog waveforms. The results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating optimized TinyML models into wearable platforms for real-time ECG analysis.

papers.title: Tangent incompleteness under coupled image transformations: margin reconstruction and decision consequences
papers.summary: Can accurate responses to individual geometric image transformations recover their combined effect on a classifier's decision? For identity-aligned bilinear resampling, coordinatewise assembly may fail at first order. Projecting the implemented transformation onto a fixed logit-margin gradient, we derive a linear term plus signed absolute-value ridges. An exact even--odd identity and ridge-cancellation conditions characterize the missing information. Under independent parameter laws, a noncancelling off-coordinate ridge obstructs even unrestricted additive fits. The coupled correction has $O(s^2)$ projected error, versus a possible $\Theta(s)$ axiswise defect; transfer to realized network margins requires local smoothness. Projected RMS errors fall by 82.96% on CIFAR-10 and 82.38% on ImageNetV2 relative to axiswise assembly; realized fixed-pair margin RMS errors fall by 39.75% and 42.73%. The representation prospectively identifies nine strict nonadditive network-margin sign configurations and permits exact minimization of a three-parameter threat surrogate, with conditional selection-regret guarantees. In an independent CIFAR-10 search, coupled-selected transformations uncover 51 top-1 changes versus 41 for axes. On 256 independent ImageNetV2/ConvNeXt-Tiny images and 16,384 transformed decisions at the prespecified scale $s=.40$, multiclass top-1 flip-prediction errors fall from 11.97% to 10.23% (paired improvement 1.74 percentage points; 95% interval [0.93, 2.61]). Directional finite differences are slightly more accurate (10.00%) at higher measured model-construction cost. These results connect first-order sampling interactions to margin reconstruction, decision prediction, and threat selection, without claiming finite-scale network certification.
papers.title_ja: 結合画像変換下での接線不完全性：マージン再構築と決定への影響

papers.title: WISP: Composable Representations for Wrist-Worn Activity Recognition
papers.summary: Smartwatches and fitness bands are among the most common wearable devices, and large national health studies record movement at the wrist. Yet existing human activity recognition benchmarks mix sensors worn on different parts of the body, so they do not show how well activities can be recognised from the wrist alone. We introduce WristHARBench, a benchmark that standardises participant-disjoint evaluation across nine wrist-acceleration datasets and two additional multichannel inertial datasets. We hypothesise that different human activities leave complementary patterns in wrist motion, such as local shape, rhythm, temporal order and cross-axis relationships, and propose WISP (Wrist-Informed Space of Predictive Representations), a composable representation space that combines representations of these patterns with compatible classifiers. Across the nine primary datasets, WISP with random search achieves 70.20% mean Macro-F1, compared with 59.62% for the strongest of 18 external baselines. Controlled ablations and baseline comparisons indicate that recognition improves mainly when a representation adds motion patterns that the others lack, rather than when it represents the same pattern in a different way.

papers.title: SONATI: Spatio-temporal ocean neighbourhood asymmetric transformer for imputation of sparse, tabular data with uncertainty
papers.summary: Missing value imputation is often a prerequisite for downstream analyses. In oceanography, observational data are frequently structured in a tabular manner, highly sparse and exhibit spatio-temporal structures that classical imputers such as k-nearest neighbours or MissForest are not suited to exploit. We present the Spatio-temporal Ocean Neighbourhood Asymmetric Transformer for Imputation (SONATI), a masked, factorised time-space transformer operating on pre-computed, local time and space neighbourhoods, which reduces computational complexity compared to global attention. SONATI is designed to work with tabular data and is thus in principle able to work on both gridded and unstructured data, though evaluation here was performed on gridded North Atlantic data only. It provides aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties through a negative log-likelihood loss and multiple forward passes with Monte Carlo dropout. Systematic ablations on attention type and masking strategies guided the final architecture design. The results showed that SONATI outperformed classical and transformer-based methods by at least 12.5% in terms of root mean squared error (RMSE) on a large observational oceanographic dataset with key biogeochemical and physical parameters in the North Atlantic (potential temperature, salinity, oxygen, nitrate, silicate and phosphate). Attention type and masking strategy strongly affected imputation accuracy and smoothness of the produced oceanographic fields. Best results were achieved by factorised time-space attention and combined geographic and per-sample masking. The combined masking strategy reduced the imputation error by 14.3% compared to per-sample masking only. Uncertainties were moderately well calibrated (miscalibration area at observed locations $0.074\pm0.012$) and moderately correlated with the imputation error.

papers.title: Scalable Beckmann Maps Improve One-step Generation
papers.summary: Beckmann Transport Models (BTM) learn one-step generative maps end-to-end from data, without a teacher, a distillation stage, or pretrained features. We introduce Scalable Beckmann Maps (SBM), which bring to BTM the two ingredients behind the quality of modern multistep generators: classifier-free guidance (CFG) and a training recipe that scales, while keeping sampling at a single network evaluation. CFG combines conditional and unconditional velocity or score predictions, which a Beckmann map does not have. Our guidance rests on one observation: the BTM current is a positive multiple of an autonomous denoising field, to which CFG applies as it does to a velocity. With exact denoisers this gives guided BTM. In practice we substitute the map's own conditional and null predictions for the denoisers, which requires no additional network and introduces a bias that we characterize. We show that the guided update is consistent with a guided conservation equation, and that guidance can move the boundaries between basins, sending more noise to the modes a condition favors. Trained from scratch in the latent of a representation autoencoder, SBM reaches a one-step FID of 1.6 on ImageNet 256x256 without a teacher or a feature loss, outperforming the Improved-MeanFlow baseline with 3.2x fewer FLOPs. In text-to-image generation it reaches a GenEval score of 0.86 with one network evaluation. As a world model, where we train without guidance, the recipe alone outperforms DriftWorld on all five metrics of two robot-manipulation benchmarks, with 1.9-2.8x less training compute and no pretrained auxiliary feature encoder.
papers.title_ja: スケーラブル・ベックマンマップによるワンステップ生成の改善

papers.title: Interpreting Diffusion Model Activations in Natural Language
papers.summary: Interpreting the intermediate activations of diffusion models (DMs) is key to understanding how they generate images. Existing interpretability methods for DMs provide limited support for open-ended interrogation, making it difficult to extract human-interpretable insights. We extend LatentQA, the task of answering natural-language questions about Large Language Model activations, to DM activations. We introduce the Diffusion-specific Activation Oracle (DAO), which translates DM activations into natural-language answers to open-ended questions about the ongoing generation. Our experiments show that DAO can effectively describe the content of the final image from activations at early denoising steps. Additionally, we demonstrate that DAO captures the structure of the DM's activation space well enough to steer image generation toward target attributes. Furthermore, we show that attribution patching through DAO identifies DM components that contribute to visual attributes specified in natural language. papers.title: Suppressing Chaos Without Silencing Excitable Oscillators
papers.summary: A negative Lyapunov exponent is not a sufficient goal for controlling an excitable oscillator. A gain can remove chaos by removing the excitation that the model is meant to keep. This manuscript studies that failure mode in three models: the forced FitzHugh--Nagumo neuron, the forced Aliev--Panfilov cardiac cell, and the autonomous Hindmarsh--Rose neuron. Chaos is measured by the largest state Lyapunov exponent. Excitation is measured by threshold crossings, by the excursion of the fast variable, and by the firing rate. Recovery damping, tracking of an unstable periodic orbit, Pyragas delayed feedback, and a change of the fast time scale are compared on the same chaotic regimes. In the forced models, large damping and large rate changes reach regularity by silencing the cell, while tracking and delayed feedback keep firing. In the autonomous model, recovery damping raises the firing rate several-fold instead. A classical matrix-measure bound links these outcomes to the channel through which the gain acts. A constant-metric contraction certificate coexists with substantial firing only under tracking, which subtracts a gain from the fast direction.
papers.title_ja: 発火可能な振動子の沈黙化なしにカオスを抑制する

papers.title: A world model for longitudinal health-trajectory prediction in older adults across multinational cohorts
papers.summary: Aging is characterized by continuously evolving health states, yet most existing prediction models focus on static health risk at isolated time points rather than explicitly modelling how health trajectories unfold over time. We developed a health world model based on the Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture to represent evolving health states and simulate future trajectories under specified actions. The model combines a state encoder, an action- and context-conditioned predictor, a stop-gradient target encoder, and clinical outcome heads. We trained the model on the US Health and Retirement Study (HRS) and evaluated it without refitting in the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA) and the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). Open-loop evaluation assessed discrimination and calibration for mortality and worsening of activities of daily living (ADL) and instrumental activities of daily living (IADL). In the held-out HRS test set, the areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) for mortality, ADL worsening, and IADL worsening were 0.89, 0.93, and 0.93 at the first horizon and 0.84, 0.84, and 0.85 at the fifth horizon, respectively. Predicted risks stratified subsequent outcomes across horizons. Across the evaluated horizons, mortality AUROC ranged from 0.867 to 0.881 in ELSA and from 0.796 to 0.801 in CHARLS. Simulated trajectories preserved the expected risk ordering across predefined action regimes. In counterfactual simulations, changes in lifestyle actions shifted predicted risks in directions consistent with observed associations. The model provides a framework for longitudinal risk prediction and action-conditioned simulation in older adults.

papers.title: FoGConcept: Identifying Interpretable Movement Concepts for Freezing-of-Gait Detection from Multi-Scale IMU Signals
papers.summary: Freezing of gait (FoG) is a disabling motor symptom of Parkinson's disease, characterized by an episodic inability to initiate or sustain effective stepping. Current inertial measurement unit (IMU)-based models can detect FoG accurately, but they fail to explain their predictions in terms of human-understandable movement concepts. A major contribution of this work is to identify nine human-understandable movement concepts encoded by a multi-scale FoG model, including gait initiation, rhythmic bilateral gait, trembling in place, shuffling steps, and pivot turns. These concepts recur across subjects, are functionally linked to the model's FoG decisions, and exhibit emergent specialization across short and long temporal contexts. Repeating the concept-discovery procedure on a new FoG dataset, wider temporal contexts, and a deeper backbone recovers the same comparatively stable set of movement concepts. Accordingly, we propose FoGConcept, a mechanism-based interpretability framework for learning movement concepts from multi-scale IMU signals. Domain experts independently recognize 88.9% of the identified concepts, while the proposed model achieves an F1 score of 94.2% for FoG detection. Our findings show that accurate FoG detection can be understood through human-recognizable movement patterns, providing new insight into what a detection model learns to distinguish FoG from non-FoG movement.

papers.title: Intervention-Robust VLA: Diverse Demonstrations for Robot Deployment with Safety Filters
papers.summary: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) have shown strong potential for learning complex robotic behaviors from demonstrations. However, learning safe behavior directly from data requires extensive coverage of safety-critical situations, which is often impractical in real-world settings. Test-time safety filters provide an alternative by correcting unsafe actions during deployment, but these interventions can drive the robot into states poorly covered by the training data, thereby degrading task performance. We introduce InteR-VLA, an intervention-robust framework for VLAs that leverages diverse task-completing demonstrations to broaden task-relevant state coverage and maintain competence under safety interventions. By better aligning the training distribution with safety-filtered deployment under the same data budget, our approach mitigates intervention-induced distribution shift while preserving task performance. Real-world experiments across in-distribution and out-of-distribution settings show that InteR-VLA maintains safety, increases Safe Success Rate up to 90% from 0% for nominal policies, and consistently outperforms nominal-data training on both evaluated VLAs.

papers.title: Benchmarking EEG feature families for ADHD research in children and adolescents: performance and explainability across attention tasks
papers.summary: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder varies in presentation. Diagnosis requires clinical and developmental assessment. Two serious games yielded four overlapping attention-task cohorts of 123-140 participants each. Repeated nested participant-held-out evaluation assessed recruitment-group discrimination. Exploratory paired participant-cluster bootstrap tests corrected for multiplicity in two separate families: 72 individual-task contrasts and 18 fusion contrasts. For eight configurations selected after inspecting predictive results, we explained held-out native probabilities before calibration. In the strongest task context, the highest configuration mean AUROC over three repetitions was 0.773, with a fixed-prediction 95% interval of 0.692-0.854 unadjusted for selecting the maximum. Precision, sensitivity and specificity were 0.740, 0.556 and 0.861. In that task, the paired AUROC difference for connectivity minus spectral features averaged +0.2083 across six classifiers and the common 8 s and 16 s durations, with pointwise 95% CI 0.1076-0.3072 and adjusted p = 0.0036. F4-AF4 beta-band coherence led repetition-level attribution summaries in five selected procedures and was selected in every fit. Other contexts showed weaker discrimination and less consistent retention of leading scientific inputs. No general classifier winner emerged. Connectivity and its recurring coherence input warrant independent replication, but do not justify a universal feature recommendation. These exploratory findings do not establish causal task effects, disease mechanisms or diagnostic validity.
